detail.abstract: Measuring brand value is a complex, interdisciplinary, and often intangible endeavor that has gained significant attention since the 1980s. This research note provides a focused overview of brand valuation, tracking its evolution from basic financial indicators to comprehensive models that integrate economic, marketing, and psychological insights. The analysis distinguishes between brand equity-the perceptions and behaviors creating demand-and brand value-the net present value of future cash flows derived from the brand asset. The note further explores modern influences on valuation, including digital technologies , brand architectures , and employee-driven value co-creation. While challenges such as subjectivity and inconsistent terminology persist , the ongoing development of objective, data-driven methodologies is essential for enhancing strategic decision-making and long-term competitive advantage.

title: The Impact of Ai-Driven Automation on Employee Productivity and Operational Costs in Amazon India's Warehouse Operations (2020-2025)

detail.abstract:
This research investigates the extent to which AI-driven automation has improved employee productivity and reduced operational costs in Amazon India’s warehouse operations between 2020 and 2025. The findings demonstrate that automation technologies such as Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs), Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems (AS/RS), predictive analytics, and machine-vision sorting solutions have significantly enhanced throughput capacity, workflow speed, and order accuracy across fulfillment centers. The integration of AI systems has also reduced manual walking distance, operational delays, and repetitive physical labour, contributing to measurable efficiency gains.

Survey results collected from 50 respondents across logistics-related sectors reveal strong recognition of automation benefits, with 78% reporting productivity improvements, 72% acknowledging reduced operational errors, and 68% identifying reductions in physical workload. However, the findings also highlight considerable workforce concerns: 60% expressed anxiety about potential job displacement, 54% reported increased performance pressure due to monitoring systems, and 82% indicated the need for digital upskilling — with only 38% stating that their organizations provide adequate training support. These perceptions emphasize the socio-technical complexity surrounding automation adoption. The case study of Amazon India reflects significant operational advantages post-automation, including an increase from approximately 100 items processed per hour manually to 300–400 items per hour with robotics, and a reduction in employee walking distance by 75–80%.

These improvements affirm that AI-enabled warehouse automation strengthens productivity and cost efficiency. Nonetheless, the research identifies the critical importance of responsible automation management, strategic reskilling initiatives, transparent communication, and human-machine collaboration to ensure long-term sustainability. The study concludes that AI-driven automation delivers substantial performance improvements but requires balanced integration that supports workforce development and ethical transformation strategies. Organizations that invest in structured upskilling programs and redesign job roles to complement, rather than replace, human labour are positioned to achieve scalable growth, maintain competitive advantage, and build a future-ready logistics workforce in India.

title: Real Estate Agents on Social Media: Evidence From YouTube Adoption
affiliations: University of Central Florida - Department of Finance, , University of Central Florida and University of Memphis

detail.title: Real Estate Agents on Social Media: Evidence From YouTube Adoption
detail.abstract: This study is the first to examine real estate agents’ adoption of YouTube, one of the most influential digital media platforms, and how adoption affects their listing and selling strategies. We first show that YouTube adopters differ from non-adopters in characteristics and business strategies. Within this group, early adopters and those who later exit the platform also exhibit distinct traits. Additionally, we find that YouTube adoption changes agent behavior, as several observable strategies shift post-adoption. The results provide new insights into how technology—specifically social media—shapes professional behavior and market dynamics in real estate.

detail.abstract: This study aims to determine the influence Green Awareness to Attitude Toward Green Product on environmentally friendly detergent products mediated by Environmental Concern, Perceived Benefit, dan Perceived Price This study was conducted on consumers of environmentally friendly detergent products in the Greater Jakarta area, involving 115 respondents. Data were collected using a questionnaire and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The results of the study show that Green Awareness has a positive and significant effect on Environmental Concern, Perceived Benefit, dan Perceived Price. These three dimensions significantly mediate the influence of Green Awareness to Attitude Toward Green Product These findings underscore the important role of consumer awareness and price perception in shaping positive attitudes toward environmentally friendly products. Practical implications of this research suggest that companies should manage price perceptions and enhance environmental education to encourage wider purchase of green products

detail.title: Social Media Marketing in Social Campaigns based on the Sport Community: A Case Study of Heart Over Distance Event
detail.abstract: This study explores how interest-based communities use social media to campaign for local initiatives, with a case study of the Sixtimeridiem running community in the "Heart Over Distance" social campaign event. This campaign aims to raise awareness of issues related to education, poverty, and local community empowerment through relay running and the distribution of humanitarian messages online. Using a qualitative approach and case study method, data were collected through semi-structured interviews and digital participatory observation, focusing on the role of social media in social campaigns. The results show that Sixantemeridiem builds emotional connections with its audience through personal narratives, consistent visuals, and community collaboration, thereby strengthening a sense of ownership of the social issues it raises. Digital interactions also encourage active solidarity among followers. This study concludes that social media marketing strategies can be an effective tool in building an open and sustainable social campaign space, not only in a commercial context. Although limited to one community and platform, these findings open the door to further exploration of multiplatform strategies and the long-term impact of digital engagement in social campaigns.

title: Theory of Change in Creative Economy Policy Making: Stakeholder Engagement, Partnerships, and Trust – A Systematic Literature Review
affiliations: Institut Teknologi Bandung (ITB), Bandung Institute of Technology, Coventry University, Coventry University and Coventry University

detail.title: Theory of Change in Creative Economy Policy Making: Stakeholder Engagement, Partnerships, and Trust – A Systematic Literature Review
detail.abstract: Creative economy policy development increasingly relies on stakeholder engagement, creative partnerships, and industry trust as fundamental mechanisms for fostering innovation and supporting creative enterprises, yet emerging evidence reveals these collaborative mechanisms can systematically impede rather than facilitate effective policy outcomes under certain conditions. This systematic literature review employed PRISMA-ScR guidelines to analyze 120 studies from the Scopus database (2015-2024) examining how traditionally facilitating elements become constraining factors in creative economy governance, using Theory of Change frameworks to identify transformation patterns and paradoxical dynamics. The analysis reveals that stakeholder engagement evolves into consultation fatigue and artistic compromise, creative partnerships generate coordination overload and accountability dilution, and industry trust produces lock-in effects that stifle innovation through predictable transformation pathways involving threshold effects, power asymmetries, and institutional inertia. Traditional Theory of Change frameworks prove fundamentally inadequate for capturing these paradoxical dynamics, with only 28% incorporating negative pathways or unintended consequences, reflecting systematic optimistic bias that overlooks how collaborative mechanisms systematically transform from facilitators into constraints. The study proposes a Paradox-Aware Theory of Change framework that acknowledges multiple concurrent pathways, incorporates threshold effects where facilitating mechanisms transform into impediments, and recognizes contextual factors influencing transformation processes, enabling policymakers to anticipate and manage the dual nature of collaborative mechanisms rather than assuming universal benefits and supporting more adaptive creative economy governance strategies.

title: Is AI Truly in Style?: A Case Study of the Public Reactions to AI-Generated Fashion Models

detail.title: Is AI Truly in Style?: A Case Study of the Public Reactions to AI-Generated Fashion Models
detail.abstract: Beyond transforming behind-the-scenes productivity and business operations, AI has started to reshape creative domains such as art, fashion, and marketing. AI-generated images are becoming more common as they saturate social media trends, and they have now been adopted into business-to-consumer campaigns, including a denim line promotion. In the August 2025 issue of a renowned American fashion magazine, advertisements featuring AI-generated models sparked controversy and debate around the human authenticity of art and the role of AI in brand communication. This paper investigates the public reception of these AI-generated models and examines how AI is perceived by the wider audience on social media. Specifically, it explores the commentaries across TikTok, where users critiqued the ads. TikTok is chosen as the main commentary ground for its clear indicators of authentic audience engagement through its metrics of likes, shares, and comments. Methodologically, the paper employs social media research and discourse analysis to assess digital reactions to fashion brands’ adoption of AI. Through this case study, the paper argues that public sentiment functions as an informal governance mechanism regulating how AI is accepted by consumers. It provides insights into how understanding the consumer base during communication campaigns is crucial for the sustainable integration of AI into industries that historically rely on cultural and artistic integrity. This study aims to contribute to debates on technology and governance by highlighting how audience reception shapes the long-term viability of AI in creative communication.

detail.abstract: We design and evaluate a socio-emotional learning (SEL) program aimed at scalable adoption in public schools in low-income settings. The intervention was implemented in a cluster-randomized trial covering 5,000 students across 136 rural Chinese primary schools. A two-year weekly curriculum, delivered by regular teachers with brief training and standardized materials, improved student socio-emotional outcomes by 0.117 standard deviations (SD). The program also raised math scores by 0.084 SD at endline and mitigated earthquake-related adverse effects for girls. At a cost of $43 per student, it offers a scalable and cost-effective SEL model for resource-constrained education systems.

title: Integration of Consumer Perception in Marketing Strategy Formulation of Stevia Based Natural Sweetener Products

detail.title: Integration of Consumer Perception in Marketing Strategy Formulation of Stevia Based Natural Sweetener Products
detail.abstract: The high awareness of healthy lifestyles among urbanites creates opportunities for natural sweetener products such as stevia. However, the level of stevia usage is still relatively low, even though 85.8% of respondents are aware of this product. This study aims to integrate consumer perceptions into the formulation of marketing strategies for stevia products using the Conjoint Analysis approach. A total of 120 respondents from Bandung and surrounding areas participated, with the majority aged 20-30 years (52.5%) and comprising workers and students. Data showed that social media was the primary source of information about stevia (45.8%), but only 38.3% of respondents had ever used it. Preference for product form shows teabags as the most preferred option (40%), and the majority of respondents stated the ideal price is below Rp50,000 (67.5%). The conjoint analysis results show that price, product form, and clean, informative packaging are the key factors influencing purchase intention. These findings are used to develop more relevant marketing strategies, including digital approaches via social media and influencers, as well as packaging that meets the expectations of urban consumers. The rising awareness of healthy lifestyles among Indonesian urban consumers presents opportunities for stevia-based natural sweetener products. Despite 85.8% of respondents acknowledging familiarity with stevia, actual usage remains low. This study integrates consumer perceptions into the formulation of marketing strategy using Conjoint Analysis. A total of 120 respondents, predominantly aged 20–30 years (52.5%) and comprising workers and students, were surveyed in Bandung and the surrounding areas. The findings highlight price (31.7%), health claims (31.7%), packaging type (19.0%), and sweetness level (17.5%) as key factors influencing purchase intention. Market simulation results suggest that products with affordable pricing, moderate sweetness, glass bottle packaging, and "zero calories" claims achieve the highest predicted acceptance. Comparisons with international studies show similar consumer emphasis on affordability and credible health claims, though taste familiarity remains a local challenge. Limitations include the relatively small, urban-focused sample, which may reduce generalizability. Future studies should involve larger and more diverse populations, longitudinal tracking, and sensory testing to capture long-term consumer adoption. These insights provide practical guidance for marketers and producers in aligning product development, pricing, and promotional strategies with consumer expectations, while also advancing consumer-based marketing approaches for functional foods in emerging markets.

title: CSR Communication and Luxury Brands: Themes for Cultivating Stakeholder-Oriented Communication on Sustainability through Social Media

detail.title: CSR Communication and Luxury Brands: Themes for Cultivating Stakeholder-Oriented Communication on Sustainability through Social Media
detail.abstract: This chapter explores how luxury brands use social media to convey their corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiatives, aiming to discern whether the content emphasizes tangible sustainability actions rather than promises. It reveals a notable trend among luxury brands toward integrated CSR communication on LinkedIn, engaging diverse stakeholders with content related to the preservation of the Planet Earth, social inclusion, and sustainable practices that include circular product design, upcycling recycling, and innovations aimed at reducing environmental impacts. Overall, our chapter contributes to luxury brand literature in exploring online communication addressing environmental and social responsibilities, with LinkedIn serving as a pivotal platform for engaging different stakeholders.

title: Seeds of Change: Unpacking the Enduring Effects of MNC Knowledge Transfer in Autonomous Social Innovation Projects by Fringe Stakeholders
affiliations: University of Turin - Department of Management, University of Turin - Department of Management,  and University of Turin

detail.title: Seeds of Change: Unpacking the Enduring Effects of MNC Knowledge Transfer in Autonomous Social Innovation Projects by Fringe Stakeholders
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the enduring effects of Corporate Social Innovation (CSI) initiatives by multinational companies (MNCs) in developing countries, emphasizing how knowledge transfer, absorption, and utilization by local fringe stakeholders foster Autonomous Social Innovation (ASI). Using an ethnographic case study of coffee farmers in the Dominican Republic, the study identifies key catalyzers—local NGO, cooperative and federation governance systems, local government, commercial institutions, and external technical actors—and enablers—awareness, cooperation, knowledge sharing, knowledge and partnership seeking—that allow ASI initiatives and the evolution of local ecosystems. Building on the literature of stakeholder engagement, stakeholder empowerment and knowledge-based view, the findings highlight how these elements collectively drive the shift from dependency-driven to self-reliant social innovation models, enabling fringe stakeholders to lead initiatives that integrate economic, social, and environmental value creation. Activities such as building training centers, developing their own branded coffee, and creating coffee tourism routes showcase the capacity of empowered stakeholders to drive impactful and scalable ASI. Our study advances the ASI literature by focusing on long-term sustainable impacts of social innovation through an egalitarian perspective of local empowered stakeholders, while previous studies largely focused on the immediate CSI impacts in a more paternalistic, MNC-based view.

title: Making Talk Cheap: Generative AI and Labor Market Signaling
affiliations: and

detail.title: Making Talk Cheap: Generative AI and Labor Market Signaling
detail.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT have significantly lowered the cost of producing written content. This paper studies how LLMs, through lowering writing costs, disrupt markets that traditionally relied on writing as a costly signal of quality (e.g., job applications, college essays). Using data from Freelancer.com, a major digital labor platform, we explore the effects of LLMs' disruption of labor market signaling on equilibrium market outcomes. We develop a novel LLM-based measure to quantify the extent to which an application is tailored to a given job posting. Taking the measure to the data, we find that employers had a high willingness to pay for workers with more customized applications in the period before LLMs were introduced, but not after. To isolate and quantify the effect of LLMs' disruption of signaling on equilibrium outcomes, we develop and estimate a structural model of labor market signaling, in which workers invest costly effort to produce noisy signals that predict their ability in equilibrium. We use the estimated model to simulate a counterfactual equilibrium in which LLMs render written applications useless in signaling workers' ability. Without costly signaling, employers are less able to identify high-ability workers, causing the market to become significantly less meritocratic: compared to the pre-LLM equilibrium, workers in the top quintile of the ability distribution are hired 19% less often, workers in the bottom quintile are hired 14% more often. * We are indebted to Adam Kapor, Jakub Kastl, and Alessandro Lizzeri for their invaluable guidance and support.

title: Can AI Replace Accountants? Data-Driven Insights into the Evolving Role of Accounting Professionals
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Can AI Replace Accountants? Data-Driven Insights into the Evolving Role of Accounting Professionals
detail.abstract: "AI won't replace accountants. Accountants using AI will." This paper examines whether artificial intelligence (AI) is replacing accountants or changing the composition of their work. Drawing on 2024-2025 industry reports and surveys, I document rapid adoption of AI for routine accounting tasks alongside rising demand for judgment-intensive work. Recent survey evidence shows 41% of accountants report using AI to automate workflows, with 64% using AI for communication tasks such as email drafting (Karbon, 2025). Empirical findings from MIT Sloan (2025) show that AI adoption shortens monthly close cycles (-7.5 days), greater report granularity (+12%), and reallocation of ~8.5% of time from routine processing to higher-value activities. At the market level, "AI in accounting" is estimated at USD 4.87 billion (2024) and projected to reach USD 96.69 billion by 2033 (CAGR ~39.6%) (Grand View Research, 2025). Meanwhile, manual invoice entry has fallen from 85% (2023) to 60% (2024), indicating substantial process automation (SAP Concur, 2024). Adoption is global: U.S. firms report widespread weekly use and further investment plans, and APAC surveys show sharp increases in workplace AI use (Wolters Kluwer, 2025). The evidence supports a nuanced conclusion: AI is not replacing accountants; accountants who adopt AI are replacing purely routine tasks while expanding their advisory and analytical roles.

detail.abstract:
Background: Workplace stress harms health and productivity; unobtrusive digital biomarkers could trigger preventive interventions. Prior work suggests—though not uniformly—that computer, especially mouse, interactions change under stress, yet most evidence stems from lab studies of acute stress. We test whether mouse features indicate momentary arousal and pleasure, and whether long-term patterns relate to chronic stress.
Method: A 7-week field study with N=87. Twice daily Affective Slider (arousal, pleasure); TICS-SSCS at baseline and midpoint. Operating-system events yielded speed, acceleration, curvature, accuracy (path deviation), clicks, scrolling, pauses, and click-induced application window switches. Features from the prior 30 min classified arousal/pleasure (low/medium/high) with random forests (10-fold CV within participants; group-wise CV holding out participants). For chronic stress, person-level mouse/usage summaries were regressed on TICS-SSCS via OLS and principal-component regression.
Results: Within participants, mouse features moderately classified arousal and pleasure (accuracy 65%, weighted F1≈0.65); high arousal was best (F1=0.74), while low was often labeled medium. Across participants, performance fell below majority-class baseline (accuracy ≈47–48% vs. ≈56–57%; weighted F1≈0.44–0.45). Chronic stress showed no significant associations: OLS yielded R^2=0.31, adj. R^2=-0.11, p=.33; PCA regression R^2=0.09, adj. R^2=0.03, p=.07; no significant components.
Conclusions: Mouse dynamics signal momentary arousal/pleasure—especially high arousal—but generic models did not transfer across users, and usage statistics did not distinguish chronic stress. Person-specific baselines and context (e.g., physiology, task) appear necessary for workplace stress monitoring.

title: Multi-Stakeholder Approach in MNEs’ Product Advertising: Evolutionary Paths of Content and Language
affiliations: University of Turin - Department of Management, University of Turin - Department of Management,  and University of Turin

detail.title: Multi-Stakeholder Approach in MNEs’ Product Advertising: Evolutionary Paths of Content and Language
detail.abstract: Purpose-Despite growing calls for practical insights on the multi-stakeholder approach in marketing and its communications, there is no empirical evidence of such kind in international advertising. This study aims to examine whether and how multinational enterprises (MNEs) have redesigned international advertising to reflect multi-stakeholder principles in language and content over time. Design/methodology/approach-We adopt a mixed methodological approach based on literature review, the Delphi method and content analysis of 258 international advertising campaigns from 86 Global Reptrak® most reputed MNEs in 2016, 2019 and 2022. Furthermore, we use the Apriori algorithm, which analyzes advertising campaigns' keyword complementarity and substitution trends. Findings-From 2016 to 2022, MNEs are gradually shifting from focusing solely on product-centered content and language to integrating broader values, such as responsibility, sustainability, humanity and ethics, which address the interests of diverse stakeholder groups in their international advertising campaigns. Research limitations/implications-Our study offers a homogeneous picture of digital international advertisements spread mainly in Southern Europe, Turkey, Canada, the United Kingdom, the United States of America and India, with no relevant differences detected in the contents and language. Future studies could replicate our analysis by including advertisements spread in other emerging countries, which we did not cover for methodological reasons. Practical implications-Our study guides marketers on integrating multiple stakeholder values into their advertisements. Originality/value-Our research provides a novel contribution to the evolution of traditional marketing communications towards a multi-stakeholder approach by identifying three main evolutionary paths for international advertising: unimodal, bimodal and multimodal communication in 2016, 2019 and 2022, respectively.

title: An Explainable and Theory-Driven Deep Learning Architecture for Consumer Search and Consideration Sets
affiliations: , New York University (NYU) - Leonard N. Stern School of Business, New York University (NYU) - Leonard N. Stern School of Business, Dartmouth College - Tuck School of Business and New York University - Stern School of Business

detail.title: An Explainable and Theory-Driven Deep Learning Architecture for Consumer Search and Consideration Sets
detail.abstract: Understanding how consumers form consideration sets is crucial for marketers, yet the complexity of modern search environments makes this challenging to capture. We develop an explainable deep learning architecture that embeds marketing theories into Recurrent Neural Networks to model consumer search dynamics during the consideration stage. A key feature of our model is that it simultaneously captures learning about both product attributes and preference weights through search, rather than learning about only one of these primitives as assumed in prior work. We apply this model to a dataset of consumers searching for smartphones, which includes attribute-level eye-tracking data and search refinement tool usage. We find that our model achieves predictive performance comparable to or better than more flexible but atheoretical deep learning models and maintains high accuracy even for small data samples. Through ablation studies, we demonstrate that these gains emerge from the synergistic integration of all model components within a theory-based framework. Leveraging our model's explainability, we show that consumers primarily learn their preference weights early in search and switch to learning product attributes about 40% into their search process. We find that greater choice complexity, while offering more options, can reduce search efficiency and lead to poorer choices.

title: AI-Enabled Symbiotic Ecosystems in Cross-Border E-Commerce: Redefining Resilience and Value Creation for Transnational Entrepreneurs

detail.title: AI-Enabled Symbiotic Ecosystems in Cross-Border E-Commerce: Redefining Resilience and Value Creation for Transnational Entrepreneurs

detail.abstract:
This article introduces the concept of AI-enabled symbiotic ecosystems as collaborative architectures where artificial intelligence (AI) integrates with entrepreneurial strategies to redefine resilience and value creation in cross-border e-commerce. Amid the 2025 e-commerce landscape exceeding $6 trillion in global revenue (McKinsey, 2025), driven by AI advancements yet challenged by geopolitical disruptions reducing GDP by 1.5% (World Bank, 2023), the primary problem addressed is the underexplored potential of AI to evolve from a tool into a symbiotic partner that co-creates value through mutual adaptation. Drawing on an integrated theoretical framework combining global value chains (GVC) theory (Gereffi, 2020), the resource-based view (RBV; Barney, 1991), social capital theory (SCT; Bourdieu, 1986), and dynamic capabilities (Teece, 2014), the study posits that these ecosystems structured through data-driven relational networks, adaptive logistical intelligence, financial predictive buffering, and innovation co-creation loops facilitate bidirectional data flows that enhance operational agility and economic multipliers in volatile markets.

Employing a mixed-methods approach, including a qualitative case study (Yin, 2018) with quantitative elements (financial audits, benchmarks from Omnisend and Klaviyo 2025 reports), the research examines a transnational e-commerce venture. Key findings reveal 15–25% enhancements in resilience, as evidenced by 277% year-over-year growth (surpassing Omnisend's 12.6% average), 38.8% customer retention (exceeding Klaviyo’s 25–30% norms), $172 average order value (19% above benchmarks), and annual economic returns over 1.5 million USD through 1:3 multipliers in jobs, taxes, and development. These outcomes validate four hypotheses, demonstrating how symbiotic AI mitigates disruptions inflating costs by 1.3 percentage points (IMF, 2025), while fostering social sustainability through inclusive growth.

The theoretical contribution lies in extending GVC models to incorporate AI as a symbiotic agent, filling gaps in actor-centric resilience for niche contexts. Practically, the framework provides a step-by-step roadmap for transnational SMBs to implement ecosystems, emphasizing agility in crises. Policy implications include scaling into international hubs, potentially unlocking billions in value by leveraging AI for equitable globalization. Limitations, such as the single-case focus and temporal bounding, suggest avenues for future longitudinal and comparative research. Overall, this work, informed by my experience scaling ventures without traditional infrastructures, advances a paradigm for resilient e-commerce, urging scholars and practitioners to harness symbiotic AI as a strategic asset in an interconnected world.

title: Assurance-Throughput in Layered AI Systems: A Technical Theory of Evidence Flow and Loss

detail.title: Assurance-Throughput in Layered AI Systems: A Technical Theory of Evidence Flow and Loss

detail.abstract: Platformized AI systems rely on layered architectures-models, orchestration, and interfaces-but the evidentiary trails needed for oversight often fracture as outputs traverse retrieval-augmented generation, routing, and tool-use pipelines. This paper develops Assurance-Throughput (AT) Theory as a technical mid-range theory of evidence flow and loss in such systems. AT distinguishes four constructs-Assurance Production (AP), Assurance Transmission (ATx), Assurance Reception (AR), and Assurance Noise (AN)-and models stakeholder-specific warranted reliance (T) as a function of how assurance artifacts (documentation, evaluations, logs, provenance credentials) are produced, transmitted across layers, received by users, auditors, and regulators, and degraded by noise. Grounded in a structured narrative synthesis, the paper articulates seven propositions that locate assurance paths and loss points, presents a concept matrix linking lifecycle stages to AT constructs, and defines throughput indices for AP, ATx, AR, and AN. These indices support an empirical agenda of reception experiments, audit-log and provenance field studies, and quasi-experiments under regulation. The theory reinterprets standards and regulatory instruments-such as the EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001 and 23894, NIST's AI Risk Management Framework, and national AI assurance guidance-as partial interventions on throughput rather than guarantees of trustworthiness. Design implications for assurance pipelines in retrieval-augmented, routed, and agentic architectures are outlined. AT offers a shared vocabulary and technical lens that connect design and governance to the normative question of when reliance on AI systems is genuinely justified.

title: Generative AI Can Improve Performance and Engagement without Harming Learning
affiliations: Boston College - Carroll School of Management, Boston College, Carroll School of Management,  and

detail.title: Generative AI Can Improve Performance and Engagement without Harming Learning
detail.abstract: We study how the usage of generative AI shapes both students' performance and long-run skill development in a large-scale field setting at a major EdTech platform. A growing literature documents that generative AI can help users complete tasks faster and more accurately when having access to the tool, but may crowd out effort and undermine skill development when used during problem-solving. In this paper, we examine a specific design in which AI is activated only after students submit an answer and is used exclusively for post-solution debriefing: analyzing mistakes, explaining solutions, and answering follow-up questions. Leveraging the partial rollout of an AI tutor across thousands of learning centers, we analyze a random panel of 19,709 students (over 2.2 million student–day observations) before and after the introduction of generative AI. A difference-in-differences design reveals that access to the AI tutor substantially increases student engagement: treated students complete 29% more sessions and 72% more problems. We also find improvements in learning efficiency, as students spend 4% less time per problem while their correctness ratio increases by 3–6%. Heterogeneity analyses show that the AI tutor disproportionately benefits lower-performing students and, at the same time, does not generate larger gains for students from higher-income areas, suggesting that the technology narrows performance gaps without widening income-based disparities. Finally, we find evidence of long-run skill development, as students with post-solution AI support convert study time into improved performance at higher rates than those without.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Malware Detection Using the MAD-25 Dataset: An Explainable Framework Bridging CNN Feature Extraction and Symbolic Reasoning

detail.title: Neuro-Symbolic Malware Detection Using the MAD-25 Dataset: An Explainable Framework Bridging CNN Feature Extraction and Symbolic Reasoning
detail.abstract: The escalating threat of malware necessitates the development of advanced detection methods. Deep learning, with its capacity to discern intricate patterns from extensive datasets, shows potential for enhancing malware detection. To accurately detect the malware, a large number of patterns and profiles are required. Apart from these, the rise of image-based malware profiles used for deep learning approaches has become essential to detect sophisticated malware. In this study, we introduce a malware image dataset, namely Malwares for Analysis and Detection (MAD-25), with Gray and RGB color image profiles (dataset), to study and analyze the malware behaviors. The dataset is meticulously crafted to represent the multifaceted nature of malware, ensuring robust and effective model training. The recent malware samples were collected from different sources such as VirusShare, VirusSign, MalwareBazaar, MalShare, theZoo, and SNDBOX. The benign binary files are collected from the internet and scanned using VirusTotal with multiple antivirus software. The ransomware (Encryptors and Locker) samples, which are very dangerous are also included for research purpose. MAD-25 samples provide unique opportunities to push the boundaries of deep learning and machine learning, paving the way for innovative research in vision-based cyber defenses, multi-class imbalanced classification, and interpretable security. The small version of the dataset is used for training, validation, and testing with several popular learning approaches. Malware detection remains a critical challenge in cybersecurity due to the rapid evolution of malware families and obfuscation techniques. Traditional signature-based methods fail to generalize against novel attacks, while deep learning models often lack explainability. To overcome, these limitations, we introduce a neuro-symbolic malware detection framework that combines image-based Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with symbolic reasoning to achieve both high detection performance and interpretability. Malware binaries are converted into images, CNNs extract salient features, and these are transformed into symbolic feature vectors for interpretable classification. Experiments on the MAD-25 dataset, consisting of ~100,000 samples spanning 7 malware families and one benign class, demonstrate high classification accuracy, robust generalization, and transparent decision-making.

title: Towards a Vendor-Agnostic AI Adoption Framework for Small and Medium-Sized Businesses

detail.title: Towards a Vendor-Agnostic AI Adoption Framework for Small and Medium-Sized Businesses
detail.abstract:
Small and mid-sized businesses (SMBs), government agencies, and universities are under increasing pressure to adopt artificial intelligence (AI) in practical, measurable ways. Artificial intelligence tools are now embedded in everyday systems, from native tools such as Microsoft 365 Copilot and Google Gemini to machine learning (ML) platforms such as AWS’s SageMaker, Google Vertex AI, and Microsoft Azure AI. Standalone tools, such as ChatGPT, Gamma.app, Canvas, and Motion further obscure the landscape of selections and safety in usage. Despite pressure to adopt AI and a seemingly infinite selection of applications, most SMBs lack a clear roadmap for evaluating options, deploying them safely, and using them effectively. Without structure, experimentation leads to fragmented initiatives, wasted investment, unnecessary data risk, and limited return on effort.

This paper introduces an AI Adoption Framework (AIAF) for SMBs. The proposed AIAF is a pragmatic framework for integrating AI into SMB operations through distinct stages to ensure business-objective-based use case selection, cultural acceptance, responsible deployment, and clear measures of success. The framework’s power is in extending the proven logic of the Cloud Adoption Frameworks (CAFs) developed by AWS, Microsoft, and Google, and translating their well-tested principles for cloud computing adoption into a structured method for adopting AI in resource-constrained environments. It also aligns with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (RMF) and follows Agile principles to ensure safe, iterative implementation.

The framework follows five phases: Align, Enable, Plan, Deploy, and Sustain. The framework outlines defined activities, deliverables, key performance indicators (KPIs), and adoption hurdles at each stage that confirm readiness to move forward. Together, these steps help SMBs leverage industry best practices to implement AI to achieve tangible business outcomes through improving employee efficiency, enhancing customer experiences, increasing marketing ROI, and raising customer lifetime value. The result is a structured yet lightweight approach any SMB can use to realize value from AI safely and efficiently.

The overarching goal of this white paper is to introduce the initial outline of a framework that can be adapted widely by SMB leaders, AI and cloud computing service providers, and their partners, and other stakeholders. This is not intended to be a final or complete framework for deployment, but rather to initiate and organize the conversation introducing, evaluating, piloting, and refining a framework to guide intentional, responsible, and safe adoption of AI and machine learning for SMBs.

title: When Laws Contradict Themselves: A Quantitative Audit of U.S. Tax Code Coherence

detail.title: When Laws Contradict Themselves: A Quantitative Audit of U.S. Tax Code Coherence
detail.abstract: Problem. Complex legal systems accumulate internal contradictions that undermine fair enforcement and consistent compliance. Why it matters. We currently lack quantitative methods to measure where and how severely statutory authorities conflict-making prioritization of legislative fixes nearly impossible. What I built. I developed CALE-LAW, a neuro-symbolic framework that computes contradiction probability (C), ambiguity entropy (H), and system-level coherence (κ) across legal authorities, with impact scoring (Δκ) to identify high-leverage clarifications. Key finding. Applied to simulated U.S. tax code sections, the system identified authority pairs with C>0.70 and H>0.95, demonstrating that fundamental definitional conflicts (e.g., income thresholds for different programs) create enforcement impossibilities-not mere complexity.

detail.title: Predicting Item Liquidity in C2C Markets: A Multi-Task Graph Neural Network Framework
detail.abstract: In customer-to-customer (C2C) marketplaces, predicting item liquidity, the likelihood and speed at which a listed product sells, is a crucial task for improving pricing strategies, recommendation systems, and overall market efficiency. Accurate prediction is particularly challenging in online second-hand business scenarios, due to extensive data censoring, high item heterogeneity, low transaction volumes, and complex competitive relationships. To address these challenges, we propose a novel multi-task graph neural network framework that jointly models item liquidity and user engagement behaviors. A key innovation is the Asymmetric Competitive Pressure Graph Convolution (ACPG-Conv) layer, which captures heterogeneous inter-item relationships by integrating a competition pressure scoring network with an asymmetric attention mechanism, producing competition-aware item representations. The framework further leverages multi-task learning, using dense user engagement signals to supervise the sparse primary survival prediction task. Experiments on real-world C2C datasets across multiple item categories show that our framework consistently outperforms alternative baselines. The results highlight the importance of jointly modeling asymmetric competition and multi-task interactions for robust, accurate, and interpretable liquidity predictions, offering actionable insights into the competitive dynamics of online second-hand marketplaces.

The recommendation on strategy is given to aid industries in implementing scalable solutions using AI. Based on case studies and secondary data, it suggests a tailored DevOps-MLOps framework, which enables continuous training feedback loops and responsible AI. detail.abstract: In today's digital era, social engineering has emerged as one of the most critical cybersecurity threats, focusing on manipulating people rather than exploiting technological flaws. Instead of targeting software vulnerabilities, cybercriminals leverage human emotions and behavior to deceive individuals into revealing confidential information, granting unauthorized access, or performing harmful actions often without realizing it. With the rise of remote work, social media, and online communication, these attacks have grown both in frequency and sophistication. This study explores major social engineering techniques such as phishing, pretexting, baiting, and impersonation, emphasizing how attackers exploit trust, fear, urgency, and curiosity to manipulate their victims. detail.abstract: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development promised a historic transformation of global development governance through its universal, integrated, and inclusive framework. Yet, a decade into implementation, the Agenda's transformative potential remains largely unfulfilled. This paper interrogates the political economy of the 2030 Agenda, examining how structural asymmetries in global governance and financing have limited its capacity to address inequality and sustainability. Drawing on a documentary content analysis of global SDG progress reviews, High-Level Political Forum (HLPF) reports, and United Nations synthesis documents (2016-2024), the study traces how the Agenda's technocratic emphasis on indicators and voluntary reporting diluted its political and redistributive dimensions. The analysis reveals a persistent gap between the normative ambition of transformation and the institutional reality of incremental adaptation. The paper argues that the 2030 Agenda's implementation model reproduces the very hierarchies it sought to overcome, leading to a depoliticisation of development. It concludes by suggesting pathways for re-embedding accountability, multilateral commitment, and structural reform in future global development agendas.

title: The Optimal Work-Rest Decision as a Threshold Policy

detail.title: The Optimal Work-Rest Decision as a Threshold Policy
detail.abstract: The decision to work or rest represents a fundamental trade-off between productivity and well-being. While ubiquitous, the principles governing the optimal timing of this cycle are not well-formalized. This paper casts this decision as a problem in optimal control theory to derive the mathematical structure of the optimal policy. Our model demonstrates that the optimal strategy is not arbitrary but is a deterministic threshold policy. We prove that it is optimal to engage in work until a state variable representing cognitive capacity depletes to a precise, critical level, R ∗ . At this threshold, the optimal action switches to rest until capacity is fully restored. We derive the analytical condition that defines this threshold, showing how it emerges from the interplay between a task’s reward, an agent’s aversion to fatigue and the dynamics of cognitive depletion and recovery. This framework provides a first-principles foundation for the calculus of human effort and yields quantitative, testable prescriptions for the structure of a sustainable and maximally productive work-rest cycle.

Central banks and financial regulators worldwide are seeking a digital-currency model that protects citizen privacy under GDPR while enforcing FATF, AML, sanctions, and cross-border rules in real time. Existing CBDC and stablecoin designs still rely on central databases and institutional monitoring, raising long-term surveillance and governance concerns.

This research presents a policy-aligned architecture—consistent with BIS and IMF guidance—that embeds GDPR Articles 5, 6, 7, 25, 30, 32 and FATF Recommendations 10, 15, 16 directly into every CBDC or regulated stablecoin transaction. Using Virtual Identities and Jurisdiction Tokens, the system enforces lawful purpose, consent, expiry, and jurisdictional controls at the protocol layer, supported by a lightweight cryptographic rule that verifies each transaction independently without exposing personal data.

The framework is directly relevant to the Digital Euro initiative, the eCNY model, regulated global stablecoins, ECB consultations, Federal Reserve research, and ongoing EU Commission and EU Parliament debates. title: Adjusted Gross Domestic Product (Adjusted GDP)

detail.title: Adjusted Gross Domestic Product (Adjusted GDP)
detail.abstract: Traditional GDP treats education as "consumption" and cash subsidies as "growth," leading to policy distortions. This paper proposes an adjusted GDP (Adjusted Gross Domestic Product), whose core formula is: government investment is limited to total tax revenue (T), excluding pure transfer payments (TRₚᵤᵣₑ), and includes only actual welfare service expenditures (R). Empirical analysis based on Taiwan data from 2010-2024 shows that the adjusted GDP is on average 84.6% of traditional GDP, with an average annual growth rate of 2.1% (compared to 2.8% for traditional GDP), indicating that traditional GDP is overestimated by 15.4%. detail.title: The Long-Run Effects of Remote Work on U.S. Office Markets
detail.abstract: We study how remote work and tighter financial conditions reshape the long-run value of U.S. office assets using micro-geographic data. We estimate tract-level office supply elasticities and build a spatial equilibrium model that links firms' input choices, workers' location choices, and office developers' financing constraints. The model explains the observed flight to quality: as remote work raises productivity, office demand shifts toward high-productivity locations, while financial frictions amplify price gaps and limit new construction. Using the model's rent predictions, we estimate long-run reversion values. In Manhattan, model-implied prices are 30-50% below pre-pandemic levels, suggesting that office valuations have not yet fully adjusted to the new spatial and financial equilibrium.

detail.abstract: The American Water Works Association's (AWWA) State of the Water Industry (SOTWI) survey provides a structured, longitudinal assessment of professional outlook, yet its relationship to financial market valuations has not been examined. This study evaluates whether professional sentiment aligns with and predicts water sector financial performance from 2004 to 2025. We analyze correlations between SOTWI scores and annual stock and exchange-traded fund (ETF) valuations, test lead-lag relationships to assess predictive content, and apply regression models and composite sentiment indices to quantify explanatory power. Results show strong positive correlations between SOTWI scores and annual stock valuations across all ten water utilities and water-focused ETFs (r = 0.47–0.74, p < 0.05). Eight of ten securities exhibit significant predictive relationships, with SOTWI explaining up to 40% of next-year valuation variance. Composite sentiment indices confirm robustness. Professional outlook aligns with long-term market valuations but not short-term returns, indicating SOTWI captures fundamental sector conditions relevant to investors.  These results provide the first empirical evidence linking professional outlook to financial market performance in the water utility sector. The findings have direct implications for utility capital planning, investor decision-making, and regulatory policy. More broadly, they suggest potential for integrating engineering-based professional assessments into infrastructure finance frameworks across utility sectors.

Employing a mixed-methods sequential explanatory design, the research incorporates surveys, interviews, and document analysis involving universities, vocational colleges, employers, and students in Dar es Salaam, Arusha, and Mwanza. Findings reveal that 85% of HLIs have revised curricula to prioritize STEM, digital literacy, and soft skills. However, implementation remains uneven, constrained by limited resources, weak industry collaboration, and bureaucratic obstacles.

Work-Integrated Learning (WIL) initiatives, such as internships and apprenticeships, demonstrate potential, with 78% of students participating. Yet, only 52% find these experiences relevant to their fields. Industry partnerships, valuable for curriculum relevance and innovation, are predominantly concentrated in urban areas, exacerbating regional disparities. Career guidance and entrepreneurship support are underdeveloped, limiting their impact on employment outcomes and self-employment pathways.

The study concludes that effective policy implementation necessitates enhanced institutional capacity, stronger industry linkages, equitable resource allocation, and the integration of practical training and entrepreneurial education. These measures are essential for bridging the education-employment gap and advancing Tanzania's transition to a knowledge-based, middle-income economy in alignment with Vision 2050.

title: The Role of Strategic Leadership on Economic Diversification and Non-Oil and Gas Sectors in the UAE
affiliations: Cairo University

detail.title: The Role of Strategic Leadership on Economic Diversification and Non-Oil and Gas Sectors in the UAE
detail.abstract:
This study examine the role of strategic leadership in facilitating economic diversification getting non-oil and non-gas sectors in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) going better and better. The UAE has decided to focus on diversifying its economy through the medium of national visions and strategies. The trend of the situation has has been toward the building of empirical research that links the country's vision with leadership practices that take place within organizations.
This study employs a quantitative, descriptive-analytical, and cross-sectional research design. The study targeted various organizations in the UAE from which a total of 450 respondents representing these organizations provided the data. On the dimensions of strategic leadership, a structured questionnaire was used to collect data for the quantitative study. Five dimensions strategic orientation, human capital development, organizational culture, regulatory oversight, and ethical practices were the main issues disclosed in the survey alongside indicators related to economic diversification and non-oil sectors' development. The instrument's robustness was assured by reliability and validity tests (Cronbach's Alpha = 0.969). Correlation and regression analysis were performed to find the nature of relations among variables.
The findings show that in the case of the UAE all dimensions of the strategic leadership concept are practiced with great vigor. The statistical analysis component shows that strategic leadership has a significant and positive impact on both economic diversification (r = 0.890, p < 0.01) and non-oil sector performance (r = 0.865, p <0.01). Among the human dimensions of leadership, human capital development and organizational culture were found to significantly impact, while regulatory oversight and ethical practices also made considerable contributions. Economic diversification was identified as the main source of reducing the risk of economic fluctuations, creating sustained growth, increasing employment opportunities, and improving the quality of life. 
Correspondingly, the development of non-oil sectors was attributed to supportive infrastructure, the upward trend of investments, and the good business climate. This research contributes theoretically by linking the concepts of strategic leadership theory and diversification policies in resource-rich economies, and also to the practical aspect, thus by offering policy recommendations. Such are: encouraging leadership methodologies that are based on environmental analysis, advancing the human capital of the Emirati, consolidating ethical governance, and augmenting organizational cultures that are supportive of innovation.
Findings of the study offer useful and feasible directions for decision-makers,corporate leadership, and economic strategists situated in the UAE and the GCC area as they move towards green and post-oil economies.

title: Are Investors Really Moonstruck? Lunar Phases, Returns, and Volatility in Global Equities and Cryptocurrencies

detail.title: Are Investors Really Moonstruck? Lunar Phases, Returns, and Volatility in Global Equities and Cryptocurrencies
detail.abstract: It is often said that stock market forecasters exist to make astrologers look good, a joke repeated for decades. Yet a peculiar strand of empirical finance keeps returning to the moon, and suggesting that maybe astrology could help forecasters look good. Several papers claim that equity returns are systematically higher around new moons than around full moons, as if investor sentiment carried a faint lunar rhythm. It is an awkward idea for a field that prides itself on risk premia, factor models, and informational efficiency, but a surprisingly persistent one. We revisit the “Moonstruck Investors” hypothesis that asset returns vary systematically with the lunar cycle, originally documented in equity markets by Dichev and Janes (2003) and extended globally by Yuan, Zheng, and Zhu (2006). These studies report that stock returns tend to be higher around new moons than full moons, suggesting a behavioral channel linking lunar phases to investor sentiment. We extend this line of research in two directions. First, we re‑examine lunar-cycle effects in global equity indices using daily data through 2025 for a broad set of developed and emerging markets sourced from Stooq. We construct ±3‑day event windows around new and full moons, compute cumulative log returns, and compare unpaired “new‑moon weeks” to “full‑moon weeks” using HAC‑robust (Newey–West) inference. We also study the evolution of the effect by decade. Second, we ask whether similar patterns appear in cryptocurrency markets, using daily data for ten large coins (BTC, ETH, XRP, BNB, SOL, TRX, DOGE, ADA, LINK, XLM). We compute cumulative returns and realized volatility in ±7‑day and ±3‑day non‑overlapping windows around new and full moons, and compare these to unconditional rolling-window benchmarks. For equities, we find no robust global lunar anomaly. Across major developed indices (S&P 500, DAX, FTSE 100, TSX, CAC 40, Hang Seng, FTSE Straits, KLCI, etc.), average 7‑day returns are slightly higher around new moons than full moons, but differences are small and not statistically significant. However, a few markets exhibit economically and statistically significant new‑moon premia: ● The Nikkei 225 (Japan) shows a new‑minus‑full difference of roughly +0.33 percentage points per ±3‑day window, with a HAC p‑value around 0.01 over the full sample. ● Two additional indices, ^SNX and TASI, display new‑moon premia of about 0.5–0.6 percentage points, with p‑values around 0.01–0.02. ● The Jakarta Composite (JCI) exhibits a particularly strong new‑moon premium in the 2000s decade (~0.9 percentage points per window, p ≈ 0.03), and borderline significance in the full sample. Decade‑by‑decade decompositions show that these effects are not time‑invariant: they cluster in specific markets and periods (e.g., S&P 500 in the 1950s, SNX and JCI in the 2000s), while other markets and decades display weak or even reversed patterns (e.g., CAC 40 in the 1960s). For cryptocurrencies, we find at best weak support for a lunar‑phase effect in returns and no evidence in volatility. In ±7‑day (14‑day) windows, both new‑moon and full‑moon periods exhibit large positive average returns consistent with the strong upward drift in crypto, and differences between phases are small and statistically insignificant. In ±3‑day (6‑day) windows, pooled returns are modestly lower around new moons and modestly higher around full moons: new‑moon windows underperform unconditional 6‑day windows by about 1.1 percentage points (p ≈ 0.02), while full‑moon windows outperform new‑moon windows by about 1.7 points (p ≈ 0.07). However, realized daily volatility in ±3‑day windows is around 4.6–4.7% per day and is virtually identical across lunar phases and relative to unconditional weeks. Taken together, our cross‑asset evidence suggests that any lunar‑phase anomaly is modest, local, and regime‑dependent. Some equity markets, notably Japan and certain emerging markets, show persistent new‑moon premia, but a broad, universal effect is not supported. In cryptocurrencies, lunar effects in returns are small relative to background drift and volatility, and there is no corresponding volatility pattern. If investors are “moonstruck,” it is in narrow pockets rather than globally.

title: Predictability and Drivers of Free-Price Events in Great Britain's Electricity Market: A 2024 Price -Carbon Analysis
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Predictability and Drivers of Free-Price Events in Great Britain's Electricity Market: A 2024 Price -Carbon Analysis
detail.abstract: Periods in which wholesale electricity prices fall to zero or below (here termed free-price events) are becoming increasingly common in decarbonising power systems. Understanding their drivers and predictability is essential for market design, demand response (DR) strategies, and investments in system flexibility. This study provides the first full-year empirical assessment of free-price events in Great Britain (GB) for 2024, combining 17,534 half-hourly observations of wholesale Market Index Data (MID) prices [1] with national carbon-intensity measurements [2]. We document 498 free-price half-hours (2.84% of the year; 14,940 minutes), concentrated in spring and late summer. Correlation analysis shows only weak contemporaneous coupling between carbon intensity and price (|r| < 0.20), indicating that carbon levels alone do not explain price collapses. To identify structural drivers, we engineer calendar, diurnal, and lagged features and train a logistic regression classifier to estimate the probability of free-price conditions. The model achieves high discriminative performance (ROC AUC = 0.995; PR AUC = 0.842; Brier score = 0.028), demonstrating that free-price events are highly predictable despite their low base rate. Lagged prices, lagged carbon intensity, and hour-of-day emerge as the strongest predictors, while seasonal progression (day-of-year) captures broader patterns of renewable generation. An odds-ratio analysis corroborates these drivers and shows significant temporal asymmetries preceding price collapses. These findings indicate that free-price events in GB are neither random nor purely weather-driven; instead, they reflect systematic, they reflect systematic market and system conditions that follow consistent patterns over time. The results provide an empirical foundation for designing DR offerings, consumer automation strategies, storage scheduling algorithms, and market reforms suited to a high-renewables GB grid.

title: Information Complexity, Trust, and Retail Investors

detail.title: Information Complexity, Trust, and Retail Investors
detail.abstract: This paper provides insights into when and why retail investors are attentive to trust, focusing on the costs of processing information. We find that retail investors are only attentive to trust in the presence of complex information characterized by high processing costs. Conversely, when information is easy to understand, trust does not influence retail investors' trading decisions. Overall, our findings indicate that retail investors prefer to understand and process information themselves, but when they face burdensome information processing costs, they rely on trust as a backup for timely trading decisions. We also find that trust plays a major role in explaining why retail investors continue to trade actively in troubled information environments, which challenges rational inattention theory.

detail.abstract: This study investigates the construction and evaluation of a simple multi-timeframe trend-following strategy applied to Bitcoin. We begin with a naïve baseline model and progressively enhance it using daily-hourly trend confirmation and a trailing exit mechanism. Using BTC/USD data from Gemini Exchange between 2018 and 2025, we demonstrate how multi-timeframe structure improves stability, reduces drawdowns, and generates superior risk-adjusted performance compared to both buy-and-hold and a pure MACD strategy. detail.title: Antitrust and Industrial Policy: A Misunderstood Relationship

publicationDetails.detailsText: Columbia Public Law Research Paper Forthcoming

detail.abstract:
Antitrust and industrial policy have long been understood as separate areas of policy, handled by different officials with different priorities. Superficially they differ and are often presumed to be in conflict. This paper takes a different view. It urges policymakers to conceive of the antitrust regime as an important tool of industrial policy, particularly for dynamic, technological industries. Stated differently, it advances the view that promoting competition (through antitrust) can be an important means of enhancing national competitiveness (a goal of industrial policy). 


This is not to suggest that antitrust is a substitute for other forms of industrial policy. It instead suggests that antitrust is one tool in the toolkit for strategic economic policy, and that one should not assume that the policies are necessarily in conflict, or that one must always choose between the two. 


In the course of the argument, this paper addresses a common policy argument: that enforcing the antitrust law will invariably disadvantage the country that does it. S  Both theory and the case studies in the second part suggest the opposite conclusion: that a failure to enforce the laws can weaken an industry over the longer turn and make it vulnerable to disruption by overseas firms.

title: Cross-Sectional Momentum in Indian Equities: A Reproducible Evaluation on the Nifty-50
affiliations: University of Southern California

detail.title: Cross-Sectional Momentum in Indian Equities: A Reproducible Evaluation on the Nifty-50
detail.abstract: This paper presents a reproducible empirical study of the cross-sectional momentum anomaly within India's Nifty-50 constituents from 2012-2025. Using monthly adjusted prices, we evaluate both a baseline (equal-weighted, long-short) and an optimized (volatility-scaled, long-only) implementation. The optimized specification achieves an annualized Sharpe ratio above 3 in-sample even after transaction costs, and delivers strong out-of-sample performance (ann. return ≈ 133.6%, vol ≈ 46.1%, Sharpe ≈ 2.90, max drawdown ≈ 41.6%). These results suggest that medium-term momentum in Indian equities arises from under-reaction and sectoral trend persistence, consistent with behavioral and informational frictions documented in emerging markets.

title: Antitrust Regulatory Gap in IndiGo Airlines 2025 Fiasco : Lessons from the US and EU

detail.title: Antitrust Regulatory Gap in IndiGo Airlines 2025 Fiasco : Lessons from the US and EU
detail.abstract: India's domestic aviation sector has reached unprecedented concentration levels, with IndiGo Airlines commanding market share and a high Herfindahl-Hirschman Index, well above the 2,500 threshold indicating high concentration risk. The December 2025 operational crisis, marked by over 1,000 flight cancellations and widespread service disruptions, has intensified calls for antitrust scrutiny and raised fundamental questions about the adequacy of India's competition law framework in regulating essential infrastructure sectors. This paper provides a comprehensive policy analysis of the India's restrained approach to aviation market concentration, contrasting it with the aggressive enforcement paradigms of the U.S. Department of Justice and European Commission. Through examination of international precedents, we identify critical regulatory gaps in India's competition enforcement architecture. We argue that India's current legal framework, rather than addressing structural concerns, is ill-suited to preventing consumer harm in highly concentrated essential services. The paper contributes to competition policy discourse in emerging markets by demonstrating that efficiency-driven dominance, while economically rational, requires proactive regulatory guardrails to protect consumer welfare in network industries. Our findings have implications beyond aviation for regulatory approaches to platform markets, telecommunications, and other infrastructure sectors experiencing rapid consolidation.

title: Pre-Bunking as a Strategic Defense: A Stackelberg Model of Inoculation, Targeting, and AI Shocks

detail.abstract: We analyze the strategic deployment of "pre-bunking" as a defense against misinformation. We model the interaction as a Stackelberg game where a platform (leader) invests in inoculating a population, and a strategic misinformation producer (follower) then chooses an optimal attack level. We first establish the leader's optimal investment in a baseline binary model, identifying a sharp "deterrence tipping point" where the strategy flips from acquiescence to full deterrence. We then extend this to a continuous-effort model, which reveals a distinct "mitigation regime" where partial, harm-reducing investment is optimal. Further extensions analyze network-targeted inoculation strategies and a dynamic model where AI-driven cost reductions for attackers can render deterrence infeasible. This framework provides a formal basis for platforms and policymakers to optimize inoculation investments and design robust interventions against strategic misinformation.

detail.abstract: We develop a PCA-enhanced agent-based calibration framework to measure how baseline liquidity depth (L0) and behavioral price sensitivity (κ) jointly determine volatility persistence in equity microstructure. Using ten years of daily data for Bank Nifty constituents, we estimate bank-specific equilibrium pairs (κ * , L * 0) through a progressive grid search that matches simulated volatility distributions and PCA-extracted market structure moments. This identifies structural trading equilibria rather than statistical fit alone. We show that volatility persistence arises from feedback dominance: when sensitivity loads exceed liquidity buffering capacity, volatility becomes a self-sustaining regime rather than a shock response. The resulting Liquidity-Sensitivity Phase Map reveals distinct amplification, metastable, and anchored regimes across institutions. Sensitivity increases the likelihood of high-volatility states more strongly than liquidity reduces it, demonstrating a core elasticity asymmetry in microstructure responses. Market fragility is therefore not driven by liquidity scarcity but by sensitivity-driven participation loops that amplify endogenous pressure. The framework provides a parsimonious, data-grounded diagnostic for identifying stability wedges and monitoring regime risk within market structure.

title: Evaluating U.S. Economic Growth in the AI Age

detail.title: Evaluating U.S. Economic Growth in the AI Age

detail.abstract:
The article argues that headline U.S. growth in 2025 masks a deepening slowdown driven by tariff‑induced import volatility, growing wealth concentration and a speculative AI investment boom. When front‑loaded imports are smoothed across two quarters, the economy slips into a technical recession despite positive GDP headlines. Wealth is increasingly concentrated in the top decile: the richest 10 % of households hold roughly two‑thirds of total wealth, while the bottom half hold just 2.5 %. Corporate behaviour has become short‑termist; firms now return about 90 % of profits to shareholders via dividends and buy‑backs, diverting trillions of dollars from innovation and wages.

These trends are linked to the U.S. monopoly over global liquidity. Since abandoning gold convertibility in 1971, Washington has leveraged dollar dominance to finance deficits and bail out markets, expanding eurodollar liquidity and reinforcing Wall Street’s power. Companies spent 55 % of earnings on buy‑backs and 39 % on dividends between 2006 and 2015, leaving only 6 % for productive investment. As consumer spending stagnates, AI‑related capital expenditure has become the main driver of GDP growth. Multi‑billion‑dollar circular deals between Nvidia, OpenAI, Oracle and AMD involve hardware purchases and cross‑investment commitments that recycle the same funds without generating genuine productivity gains.

International competition intensifies the bubble. China’s open‑source model Kimi K2 Thinking reportedly outperforms GPT‑5, pushing U.S. firms to invest even more aggressively in AI infrastructure. The article contrasts U.S. market‑driven governance with China’s state‑guided model and argues that sustainable growth requires reining in shareholder primacy, tackling inequality and instituting rigorous AI safety and governance measures.

Conflict, especially when driven by rejection of those inequalities, can hasten reform by exposing entire systems and practices to scrutiny and revision, thereby serving as a more effective catalyst for women's political advancement.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces and validates a novel Innovation Capability Index (ICI) that captures a set of diverse innovation-related capabilities within a single empirical measure. The index is applied to health-insurance contractors participating in the U.S. Medicare Advantage program, which ties financial incentives to annual performance ratings. Using survey data from plan managers supplemented by qualitative interviews, the study finds that innovation capability is positively associated with higher performance ratings. Qualitative insights support the plausibility of multiple causal pathways, including innovation as both a response to performance incentives and a means to sustain high performance under shifting regulatory conditions. While based on a modest sample, the ICI provides a replicable and policy-relevant framework for measuring behavioral additionality, the internal capability changes induced by public policy. The approach offers a generalizable program-evaluation tool for evaluating how performance-based procurement programs may indirectly stimulate innovation.

title: Moral Rights of Authors under the Indian Copyright Act: Protection, Challenges, and Judicial Trends

detail.title: Moral Rights of Authors under the Indian Copyright Act: Protection, Challenges, and Judicial Trends
detail.abstract: This paper explores the significance and scope of moral rights under the Indian Copyright Act, 1957, emphasizing Section 57 which embodies the author's right to claim authorship and to protect the integrity of their work. Unlike economic rights, moral rights safeguard the author's personality and reputation embedded in the creative expression. The study examines the philosophical foundation of these rights, their recognition in Indian jurisprudence, and comparative insights from international conventions such as the Berne Convention. The paper particularly analyzes landmark cases including Amarnath Sehgal v. Union of India and subsequent judicial interpretations to understand how Indian courts have upheld authors' moral rights. It concludes by discussing contemporary challenges in enforcing these rights in the digital and AI-driven creative landscape.

detail.abstract: We investigate the behavior of BLS monthly revisions to payroll growth at turning points. We find some evidence corroborating claims by former BLS commissioners and market analysts that revisions around turning points tend to be procyclical and more serially correlated. Furthermore, we do see large revisions before turning points. However, the ability to use revisions to forecast business cycles' turning points seems limited. First, we do see lots of false positives: large revisions occur without a subsequent recession. Second, even within-sample, other indicators, such as initial jobless claims, the Chicago Fed National Activity Index, and the Aruoba-Diebold-Scotti Index, do a better job at detecting recessions. Finally, out-of-sample forecasting performance of revisions is poor.

title: The Political Economy of Artificial Intelligence: Automation Risk and Wage Dynamics in the United Kingdom

detail.title: The Political Economy of Artificial Intelligence: Automation Risk and Wage Dynamics in the United Kingdom
detail.abstract: Following the 2016 deep-learning breakthrough, artificial intelligence (AI) transitioned from proof-ofconcept to commercial deployment, yet its labour-market consequences remain contested. Taskdisplacement theory predicts that occupations whose tasks are easiest to automate should see wages fall, while augmentation theory expects technology-driven pay gains. Understanding how AI reshapes wage structures is vital for designing labour-market institutions that capture rather than concede the productivity dividend. Exploiting United Kingdom data, this study links the Office for National Statistics' ex-ante automation-probability scores for every four-digit occupation to a near-census panel of hourly wages from the Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings covering 2014-2023. A twoway fixed-effects specification interacts each occupation's risk score with a post-2016 indicator, using 2016 as an institutional anchor that aligns the onset of commercial deep-learning deployment with the introduction of the National Living Wage, and netting out time-invariant occupation traits and common macro shocks. The results show that occupations in the top half of the risk distribution experienced approximately three percentage points of cumulative real-wage growth relative to lowrisk occupations over 2016-2023; the positive, highly significant interaction persists when pandemic years are excluded. These findings support the augmentation narrative, suggesting that Britain's rising National Living Wage and post-Brexit labour scarcity helped workers capture part of the AI dividend. While the time-invariant risk index and short pre-AI window limit formal pre-trend testing, robustness checks confirm the core result, pointing to human-centric AI adoption as a policy priority.

detail.abstract: Technological progress is reshaping living standards at a global scale. In the 21st century, innovations are no longer confined to advanced economies-they are diffusing rapidly across developing nations, enabling "leapfrogging" of traditional development stages. This paper examines how widespread technological diffusion and societal optimization are poised to reduce poverty and transform economies, with a particular focus on Africa. We review key sectors-automation and AI, fintech, healthcare, energy, agriculture, education, and digital infrastructure-where modernization is accelerating growth and improving welfare. Evidence from recent studies and development programs shows that access to mobile broadband and digital finance has significantly raised incomes and lifted millions out of extreme poverty in Sub-Saharan Africa. Off-grid renewable energy and telemedicine are bridging critical infrastructure gaps, delivering affordable electricity and healthcare to underserved populations. Yet, these opportunities come with challenges: unequal access, skill deficits, and the risk of widening inequalities if technology's benefits are not broadly shared. Achieving the promise of inclusive modernization will require supportive policies-investment in infrastructure, education, and governance-to ensure innovations spread quickly and equitably. The 21st century will be defined not only by breakthrough technologies, but by how effectively they are harnessed to optimize societies and lift billions out of poverty.

title: Amplifying Agri-Food Sustainability Pathways: A Configurational Model of Value Chain Organizing for Contextual Fit
