Following the National People's Power (NPP) coalition's electoral victory on an anti-corruption platform, the government's proposal to procure 1,775 double cab pickup trucks for Rs. 12.5 billion sparked signi�icant political controversy. Through qualitative case study methodology, this research analyzes allegations of procurement manipulation, critiques the regressive policy shift from duty-free permits to state-owned vehicle �leets, and examines implications for political legitimacy. Drawing on institutional economics, public administration theory, and governance literature, the study reveals a critical gap between campaign promises and governing praxis. The �indings demonstrate how procedural opacity, �iscal irresponsibility, and policy reversals can rapidly erode public trust in reformist governments, offering broader lessons for post-crisis democratic transitions.

title: The Missing Middle: Behavioural Drift, Safety Risk, and the Erosion of Middle Management in Community Care Settings

detail.title: The Missing Middle: Behavioural Drift, Safety Risk, and the Erosion of Middle Management in Community Care Settings
detail.abstract: This paper examines the erosion of middle management as a source of behavioural governance in contemporary organisations. While management discourse increasingly promotes flattened hierarchies and self-managing teams, the behavioural and safety consequences of these shifts remain underexplored. Drawing on a qualitative case vignette from a community-based intellectual disability care organisation in New Zealand, the paper shows how middle management roles may persist structurally while becoming functionally weakened in practice. Integrating organisational safety and learning literature-including Reason's model of organisational accidents, Vaughan's concept of normalisation of deviance, and Edmondson's work on psychological safety-the analysis demonstrates how weakened middle management contributes to behavioural drift, declining incident reporting, and the accumulation of latent safety risks. In the absence of sustained managerial presence and reinforcement, behavioural responsibility migrates downward and becomes governed by informal power dynamics rather than professional norms. The paper argues that the erosion of middle management represents a design failure rather than an individual or cultural deficiency. Behavioural governance does not disappear when hierarchies are flattened; it is displaced. When this displacement is unacknowledged, organisations become increasingly reliant on silence and luck rather than on early detection and learning to maintain safety. The findings highlight the need to reframe middle management as behavioural infrastructure and to treat behavioural authority as a core organisational design concern, particularly in high-risk and care-based environments.

detail.abstract: As an agrarian country, Indonesia requires an efficient fertilizer distribution system to support agricultural productivity. East Java Province, as a leading food producer, needs a decision-support system to optimize fertilizer allocation and distribution. This research develops a decision-support system based on the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) and the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) to optimize fertilizer distribution in East Java. The system considers eight criteria: land area, urea allocation, urea distribution, ZA allocation, ZA distribution, NPK allocation, NPK distribution, and primary commodities. Data used in this study include the Dataset Alokasi Distribusi Pupuk Provinsi Jawa Timur 2023–2024 (Fertilizer Allocation Dataset of East Java Province 2023–2024), Dataset Salur Distribusi Pupuk Provinsi Jawa Timur 2023–2024 (Fertilizer Distribution Delivery Dataset of East Java Province 2023–2024), Luas Panen Padi Menurut Kabupaten/Kota 2024 (Rice Harvested Area by Regency/City 2024), agricultural land area in East Java (luas lahan pertanian di Jawa Timur), and the Harvest Area, Production, and Productivity of Corn and Soybeans by Regency/City in East Java Province (luas panen, produksi, dan produktivitas jagung dan kedelai menurut kabupaten/kota di Provinsi Jawa Timur). Research results show that the AHP-TOPSIS system can provide accurate rankings of fertilizer distribution priorities based on predetermined criteria. This system can help decision-makers optimize resource allocation and improve the efficiency of the fertilizer supply chain in East Java.

title: The Correlation Between Corruption and Weak Human Development
affiliations: Bakrie University

detail.title: The Correlation Between Corruption and Weak Human Development
detail.abstract: Corruption remains a persistent obstacle to sustainable human development, particularly in developing countries. It undermines public service delivery, weakens institutions, and reduces the effectiveness of policies aimed at improving education, health, and social welfare. Conversely, weak human development may also reinforce corruption.  This study investigates the relationship between corruption and human development using a quantitative correlation approach. The analysis is based on a dataset comprising 199 data points from 75 countries, covering the period from 2013 to 2022. Four key indicators are utilized, namely the Corruption Perception Index (CPI), Human Development Index (HDI), PISA scores, and the Economist Intelligence Unit’s Democracy Index. The findings indicate a fairly strong and statistically significant negative correlation between corruption levels and human development outcomes. Higher corruption is consistently associated with lower HDI scores, weaker educational performance (as measured by PISA), and diminished democratic quality. These results highlight a reciprocal relationship, where high levels of corruption hinder human development, and weak human development environments in areas such as education and governance create conditions that allow corruption to thrive. The study concludes that embedding integrity-based education constitutes a normative foundation for breaking the vicious cycle of corruption and advancing sustainable human development.

title: Communication, Culture, and Media in the Digital Era: The Case of Sound Branding in Destination, Rammang-Rammang Geosite, South Sulawesi

detail.title: Communication, Culture, and Media in the Digital Era: The Case of Sound Branding in Destination, Rammang-Rammang Geosite, South Sulawesi

keywords.keywords: Communication; Culture; Media; Sound Branding; Geotourism; Geosite Rammang-Rammang

detail.abstract: In the digital era, communication, culture, and media converge on multimodal platforms where meaning is shaped not only through text and image but increasingly through sound. While communication research has long emphasized the visual turn (Rose, 2016; Manovich, 2020), emerging scholarship highlights sound as a formative communicative resource that encodes affect, identity, and cultural memory (Sterne, 2012; Bull, 2000). Building on this shift, this study examines how natural soundscapes become strategic assets for destination communication and branding within geotourism. Rammang-Rammang Geosite in South Sulawesi offers an illuminating case: its immersive sonic environment—limestone echoes, mangrove rustling, endemic bird calls, and profound silences—constitutes a cultural text through which the landscape is sensed and interpreted. Empirical findings from Murtadha (2025) show that visitors associate these auditory patterns with tranquility, awe, and place-belonging, whereas intrusive anthropogenic noise disrupts affective engagement. These insights align with Schafer’s (1994) notion of soundscape and Clynes’s (1977) Sentic Theory linking acoustic patterns to embodied emotional response. The study further demonstrates that sound branding extends beyond on-site experience into digital mediation. Recordings circulating through social media and tourism platforms translate local auditory identity into a globally legible narrative, while simultaneously raising concerns about the commodification of ecological sounds. When practiced responsibly, however, digital sound branding can support conservation-oriented communication by foregrounding silence, natural rhythms, and ecological fragility as elements of sustainable tourism storytelling (UNESCO, 2021). Ultimately, Rammang-Rammang illustrates that sound branding is not merely a marketing technique but a communicative practice rooted in ecological experience and cultural meaning-making, generating narratives that are both embodied and digitally resonant

detail.title: Cooperation in a Dynamic Network
detail.abstract: We study the scope for cooperation in an evolving network. Under endogenous dynamics, cooperation leads to a growing neighborhood of long-term productive relationships, while defection exploits ephemeral relationships resulting in social marginalization. We characterize a class of simple stationary equilibria in which, even as players become patient, the coexistence of cooperation and defection naturally arises. This captures the observation that many social networks are characterized by a high, though not universal, level of cooperation.  Low levels of cooperation can be sustained only through exclusivity among cooperating agents.

detail.abstract:
The rapid and enthusiastic interest in development and deployment of Agentic AI and especially autonomous agents which are capable of independent reasoning, leveraging and  executing tools, has outpaced the definition of governance mechanism that is required to manage their operational, ethical and regulatory risks.There are existing AI governance models like NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, do provide foundational controls however, they are very generic and lack the implementation depth for these conitnuously acting, multi-agent systems.

This paper introduces The Agentic AI Governance Framework, which is a six principled lifecycle model designed to ensure traceability, accountability, and regulatory alignment across agentic deployments. The framework formalizes quantifiable controls through two applied mechanisms: the Agentic Log Retention Index (ALRI), which defines evidenceretention periods based on agent risk and jurisdiction, and a Runtime Governance Architecture integrating human-in-loop escalation, tool-access allow-lists, and modelprovenance capture. Implementation mappings are provided for major orchestration environments including LangChain, Power Platform, and UiPath. 

Adoption of the framework enables organizations to reconstruct agentic decisions within 24 hours, achieve ≥ 95 % provenance coverage, and detect behavioral drift within 10 % variance. The proposed model bridges the current gap between compliance principles and deployable governance practice, establishing a reusable baseline for safe and auditable Agentic AI operations.

keywords.keywords: Short-time work; employment; wages; unemployment insurance.

publicationDetails.journalName: National Bank of Belgium Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We evaluate the effectiveness of Belgium’s short-time work (STW) program during the Great Recession, a period when the country recorded the highest STW take-up rate in Europe. STW allows firms to reduce working hours in response to temporary shocks while avoiding layoffs, playing a key role in European labor market insurance systems. Using an instrumental variable strategy that exploits quasi-exogenous variation stemming from an institutional feature of the Belgian program, we estimate the causal effects of STW on employment and wages. We find that, while STW significantly reduces the volume of work per worker, it does not lead to statistically significant employment gains for the average treated firm. Importantly, positive employment effects are concentrated among small manufacturing firms, which are more likely to face binding liquidity constraints. These findings highlight the importance of targeting and screening in improving the cost-effectiveness of STW programs and minimizing deadweight losses.

title: Startup Dynamics in Indonesia: Leveraging Lean Startup and Dynamic Capabilities for Growth and Sustainability

detail.title: Startup Dynamics in Indonesia: Leveraging Lean Startup and Dynamic Capabilities for Growth and Sustainability
detail.abstract: This study examines the development trajectory of digital startups in Indonesia by integrating Dynamic Capabilities Theory and the Lean Startup methodology. Employing a qualitative case study approach, we conducted semi-structured interviews with twelve senior executives and ecosystem enablers across fintech and healthtech sectors to explore how early-stage ventures navigate critical developmental phases. The research identifies six distinct stages of startup development—ideation, pre-seed, seed, launch and growth, maturity, and exit strategy—each characterized by unique challenges and strategic imperatives. Our findings reveal that successful startups leverage dynamic capabilities through iterative learning, rapid MVP experimentation, and continuous market feedback adaptation to achieve product-market fit despite resource constraints and regulatory uncertainties. The study highlights the instrumental role of Indonesia's startup ecosystem, particularly incubators, accelerators, and government initiatives, in providing critical resources and mentorship that enhance survival rates. However, significant challenges persist, including uneven geographic distribution of support services, suboptimal incubator effectiveness, and regulatory ambiguities. The research demonstrates that integrating dynamic capabilities with Lean Startup practices enables startups in emerging economies to overcome institutional challenges by enhancing sensing, seizing, and transforming capabilities. These findings offer valuable insights for policymakers designing supportive frameworks and practitioners seeking sustainable growth strategies in Indonesia's rapidly evolving digital economy.

title: A Comprehensive Legal Analysis of the Regulation on a Unified Digital Identity: Implications for Strengthening Legal Accountability among Indonesian Citizens

detail.title: A Comprehensive Legal Analysis of the Regulation on a Unified Digital Identity: Implications for Strengthening Legal Accountability among Indonesian Citizens
detail.abstract: The advancement of technology has positioned social media as a primary necessity, primarily serving as a medium for communication and information exchange. Among the most widely used platforms in Indonesia are Instagram and TikTok. However, the widespread use of social media has also given rise to various negative phenomena, including hate speech, the spread of disinformation (hoaxes), threats, doxing, and cyberbullying. A significant challenge in addressing cybercrime is identifying perpetrators, often due to the use of fake accounts and online anonymity. Anonymity, therefore, becomes a root issue, enabling individuals to act with impunity and without fear of legal consequences. In response, the Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs has proposed regulating a Single Digital Identity (Identitas Digital Tunggal/IDT), which would limit each person to a single social media account. This measure is designed as a strategic initiative to protect the public from cybercrime and promote user accountability. Nonetheless, such a policy may affect citizens' constitutional right to freedom of expression, raising a fundamental tension between legal protection and civil liberties. This study aims to provide a juridical review of the constitutional position of the right to freedom of expression on social media, based on the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and relevant legislation, including Law No. 1 of 2024 concerning the Second Amendment to Law No. 11 of 2008 on Electronic Information and Transactions (ITE Law). Employing normative juridical research and secondary data, this study finds that while freedom of expression on social media is constitutionally protected, its exercise is subject to limitations under statutory law, particularly the ITE Law, which prohibits specific categories of content.

Food security refers to people’s access to enough safe nutritious food in order to be able to lead a healthy active life. It also involves elements such as food availability and affordability, as well as people being able to access food that can be consumed healthily. Natural disasters, however, can seriously threaten food security. Disasters’ effects on food security are especially more evident in countries such as Türkiye that are frequently exposed to natural disasters due to their geologic and geographical structure. For this reason, the study investigates the effects of natural disasters on food security in Türkiye. The research first creates the Food Security Index in order to estimate the effects of natural disasters on food security. The next phase follows the process of econometric analysis, which consists of three steps. Step one of the econometric analysis uses unit root tests to check the stationarity levels of the series. The second step uses the autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) bounds test to examine the long-term relationship between natural disasters and food security. The third and final step estimates the effects of natural disasters on food security. According to the obtained results, the study shows earthquakes, storms, and floods to have a significant short- as well as long-term negative effect on food security. The overall impact of natural disasters on food security has also been determined to be negative.

The study employed purposive sampling and analyzed 168 data points covering 56 regencies/municipalities across three years (2022–2024). detail.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of system quality, ease of use, and data security in technology-based tax systems (Coretax) on tax transparency among tax consulting firms in the Greater Jakarta area (Jabodetabek). As digital transformation continues to reshape public administration, understanding the role of technological features in enhancing transparency is critical. A quantitative research approach was employed, using a structured questionnaire distributed to tax consultants operating within the Jabodetabek region. The collected data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS software to assess the relationships among the independent variables (system quality, ease of use, and data security) and the dependent variable (tax transparency). The findings reveal that system quality and ease of use significantly influence tax transparency, suggesting that user-friendly, efficient systems foster more transparent reporting and greater trust. Additionally, data security contributes to taxpayer confidence in using Coretax platforms. These results emphasize the importance of enhancing system reliability, simplifying user interfaces, and strengthening data protection measures to optimize transparency in tax administration. The study offers valuable insights for policymakers and tax consulting firms seeking to improve accountability and public trust through digital tax platforms.

detail.abstract: The energy industry plays a crucial role in national economic growth and energy security. These adaptive practices enable the company to maintain credibility, strengthen stakeholder trust, and mitigate reputational risks in a dynamic information environment. The study concludes that corporate reputation in the digital era depends not only on operational achievements but also on consistent, transparent, and data-driven communication strategies. This research contributes to the understanding of adaptive PR practices and provides a benchmark for energy companies and other industries facing similar challenges of digital disruption. detail.abstract: This study assesses the effect of informal sector activities on urban household income in Chiro Town, Ethiopia. As a critical yet underexplored livelihood source in emerging towns, the informal sector's role is analyzed through a cross-sectional study of 288 households selected via a multistage sampling technique. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression. The findings indicate that participation is primarily driven by a lack of formal employment (61.1%), with major constraints being a shortage of working space, unstable customer demand, and complex licensing. Regression results reveal that household income is significantly influenced by the type of informal activity. Compared to street vending, engagement in the service sector has a strong positive effect on income (B=934.307, p=0.001), while construction work has a significant negative effect (B=-900.507, p=0.007). Furthermore, being female, working more hours, and having more experience positively affect income, whereas larger family size and older age suppress it. The study concludes that the informal sector is an indispensable survival mechanism that exhibits significant internal economic stratification. We recommend targeted interventions, including sector-specific skills training, simplified formalization processes, and the provision of secure workspaces and credit access, to enhance the sector's productivity and its contribution to household welfare.

title: The Foundations of Policy: The Hidden Equation of Government

detail.title: The Foundations of Policy: The Hidden Equation of Government
detail.abstract:
Foundations of Policy is an inquiry into the hidden order of human behavior that governs every act of governance. Its central insight—that all policy outcomes can be decomposed into what people are able to afford and how they adapt—derives from the Slutsky Equation, first formulated in 1915 and refined by Hicks, Shephard, Hotelling, and Friedman. Through this simple but universal logic, the book reveals why so many well-intentioned reforms fail: compassion collides with consequence, and virtue outruns reason.

Drawing on three decades of fieldwork as an economic adviser to emerging post-Soviet governments and later as director of U.S. reconstruction efforts in Kosovo, Afghanistan, Iraq, and beyond, Stephen Lewarne shows that the same structural errors that undermine policy in fragile states recur across modern democracies. Whether in rent control, minimum-wage laws, diversity mandates, climate policy, or social welfare design, policymakers repeatedly mistake first-round effects for final outcomes, neglecting the behavioral substitutions that quietly undo their aims.

Foundations of Policy is not a new theory of economics but a synthesis—an attempt to bundle the vast machinery of mathematical economics into a form that policymakers and analysts can actually use. It presents a moral and analytical discipline for those who seek legacy rather than applause: a checklist rooted in equilibrium, prudence, and respect for human agency. The Slutsky framework, recast here as the grammar of governance, becomes both a mathematical and philosophical guide—showing that to govern wisely is to foresee adaptation, to let reason restrain virtue before virtue defeats itself.

title: Technology Rivalry and Resilience Under Trade Disruptions: The Case of Semiconductor Foundries

detail.title: Technology Rivalry and Resilience Under Trade Disruptions: The Case of Semiconductor Foundries
detail.abstract: This paper studies the impact of industrial policies on technology competition and consumer welfare amid rising global trade disruption risks. Distilling key empirical features from novel data on the semiconductor foundry industry, I develop and estimate a dynamic oligopoly model that integrates step-by-step innovation, trade disruption risk, and industrial policies. While distortions from market power and technological externalities justify subsidies, their optimal levels depend on the magnitude of trade disruption risk: when the risk is low, the optimal subsidy rate remains low, as the welfare benefits are distributed globally, but the costs are borne exclusively by the subsidizing government. My quantitative model shows that a 35% trade disruption risk makes the 25% investment subsidy under the U.S. CHIPS Act optimal, resulting in a 6% welfare improvement for the U.S. The paper also analyzes the CHIPS Act's restrictions on investments in rival countries, intended to secure technological leadership against their firms. Its efficacy depends on the strength of technology spillover restrictions and the scale of the rival home market secured for rival firms.

title: The impact of Economic Growth, Foreign Direct Investment and Trade Openness on Environmental Sustainability in Nigeria (1990-2023)

detail.title: The impact of Economic Growth, Foreign Direct Investment and Trade Openness on Environmental Sustainability in Nigeria (1990-2023)
detail.abstract: This study investigates the impact of economic growth, foreign direct investment (FDI), and trade openness on environmental sustainability in Nigeria, using renewable energy consumption as a proxy. Utilizing annual data from 1990 to 2023 and applying the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) approach, the research focuses on short-run dynamics to understand these relationships. Findings reveal that economic growth and urbanization negatively affect renewable energy consumption, indicating a higher dependence on nonrenewable energy sources during periods of increased GDP and urban population. In contrast, FDI, trade openness, and improved governance demonstrate positive but statistically insignificant influences on renewable energy use, highlighting the crucial role of institutional quality in promoting sustainable development. The theoretical framework combines Endogenous Growth Theory and the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis, suggesting Nigeria remains in the early EKC phase where economic growth does not yet lead to environmental improvements. Based on these results, the study recommends strengthening governance, adopting green economic policies, encouraging renewable energy investments, and managing urbanization sustainably. Limitations include the use of annual aggregate data and a narrow focus on macroeconomic variables, pointing to opportunities for future research involving higher-frequency data, regional analysis, and inclusion of technological and social factors. Overall, the study underscores the complexity of balancing economic growth and environmental sustainability, emphasizing the need for policy reforms and institutional strengthening in Nigeria.

title: Deflating "Deflation": A Conceptual Critique of Fisher, Keynes, and the Modern Fear of Falling Prices

detail.title: Deflating "Deflation": A Conceptual Critique of Fisher, Keynes, and the Modern Fear of Falling Prices
detail.abstract: This paper conducts a fundamental conceptual critique of the "deflation phobia" that has dominated modern macroeconomic thought and policy. We argue that this deep-seated fear originates from a foundational error of definition committed by Irving Fisher and uncritically inherited by subsequent generations. Our critique unfolds in three stages. First, we establish a clear demarcation between Keynes's psychological "liquidity trap" and Fisher's balance-sheet-driven "debt-deflation spiral," two distinct theories often erroneously conflated. Second, we dissect Fisher's model to expose its core flaw: the unwarranted generalization of "asset price collapse"—a financial phenomenon of relative price adjustment—into "deflation," a monetary phenomenon concerning the general purchasing power of money. This definitional error, we contend, is the "original sin" that created a false equivalence between any form of falling prices and economic catastrophe. Finally, by means of a simple "apples and gold coins" model, we reconstruct a precise taxonomy of price decline, distinguishing between malevolent monetary deflation, benign productivity-driven price declines, and relative declines. We argue that the only truly systemic danger of benign price declines lay in a now-obsolete technological flaw—the "smallest coin problem"—which has been rendered moot by the infinite divisibility of digital currency. This clarification is not mere semantics; it is a direct challenge to the intellectual underpinnings of the pro-inflationary, credit-expansionary policies of the past half-century. By demonstrating that the fear of benign deflation is no longer technologically justified, we call for an end to the "war on deflation" and a return to a sound money paradigm that embraces the rising purchasing power born of human progress.

title: Olympic Success and Gender Equality: How Media Narratives Shape Social Norms

detail.title: Olympic Success and Gender Equality: How Media Narratives Shape Social Norms
detail.abstract: Does female athletic achievement in the Olympic Games influence broader gender equality? We study this question in the context of China's return to the Olympics in 1984, combining comprehensive athlete records from 1984-2004 with detailed census data. Using a two-way fixed-effects design, we exploit variation in the timing of each prefecture's first female Olympic medal and differential exposure across cohorts who still could make education decisions versus those beyond that window. We find that the emergence of a hometown female medalist significantly reduces gender gaps in education and improves women's labor market outcomes. To address potential endogeneity in medal timing, we construct a Bartik-style instrument based on shifts in Soviet presence and relative strength across sports following the 1991 collapse of the Soviet Union, which generated exogenous variation in Chinese prefectures' medal opportunities. Mechanism analyses indicate that media framing-rather than coverage intensity-drives these effects: in People's Daily, female medalists are disproportionately portrayed through genderequality narratives rather than national pride. Together, the results suggest that publicized female achievement can challenge entrenched gender stereotypes and foster broader gender equality.

detail.title: A Protocol for Privacy-Preserving AML Compliance in CBDCs Using Virtual Identities and Jurisdiction Tokens

keywords: And Lawful-Purpose Enforcement Are Prerequisites for Public Trust

detail.abstract: Central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) must satisfy two conflicting requirements: (1) provide privacy-preserving payments for citizens, and (2) enforce financial-integrity rules such as anti-money-laundering (AML) and sanctions compliance. Existing approaches solve only one side: privacy-only constructions (e.g., ZK-based systems) provide unlinkability but lack real-time policy enforcement, while compliance-only systems rely on central databases and expose users to excessive surveillance risk. We propose a protocol that makes lawfulness a cryptographic predicate. Each transaction carries two cryptographic objects:  a Virtual Identity (VI), a pseudonymous, enclave-generated token, and  a Compliance Jurisdiction Token (CJT), signed by an authority, encoding the applicable jurisdiction, lawful purpose, consent state, expiry, and AML policy. Validators check a constant-time predicate Valid(VI, CJT, ctx) ∈ {0,1}, where ctx includes transaction metadata such as asset type, network path, and time. The protocol uses hybrid post-quantum signatures (e.g., Ed25519 + Dilithium-III) to ensure long-term security without degrading latency. We formalize security properties including identity authenticity, policy soundness, revocation-liveness, and ledger-consistent auditability, and provide security games showing that violating any policy reduces to forging signatures or producing hash collisions. A prototype implementation using eBPF/XDP demonstrates p95 < 5 ms per-transaction validation and >10M transactions/s throughput, suggesting feasibility for real-time retail CBDC rails. Our results indicate that protocol-level enforcement of privacy and AML rules is possible without compromising performance, enabling a middle path between privacy-only and surveillance-heavy CBDC architectures.

title: A Protocol for Privacy-Preserving AML Compliance in CBDCs Using Virtual Identities and Jurisdiction Tokens

detail.title: A Protocol for Privacy-Preserving AML Compliance in CBDCs Using Virtual Identities and Jurisdiction Tokens
detail.abstract:
Central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) must satisfy two conflicting requirements: providing privacy-preserving payments for citizens while enforcing financial-integrity rules such as anti-money-laundering (AML), sanctions controls, and jurisdictional restrictions. Existing approaches solve only one side. Privacy-only designs (e.g., ZK-based systems) offer unlinkability but cannot enforce real-time policy constraints, while compliance-only systems depend on central databases and risk violating key GDPR obligations—including Articles 5, 6, 7, 25, 30, 32 and cross-border rules in Articles 44–49—by exposing excessive metadata to authorities.

We propose a protocol that makes lawfulness a cryptographic predicate. Each transaction carries two objects: a Virtual Identity (VI), a pseudonymous enclave-generated credential proving lawful origin without revealing personal data; and a Compliance Jurisdiction Token (CJT), signed by an authority, encoding jurisdiction, lawful purpose, consent state, expiry, sanctions status, and AML policy. This structure satisfies FATF Recommendations 10 (CDD), 15 (new technologies), 16 (Travel Rule), and 20 (suspicious-activity reporting) at transaction time, and aligns with the BIS principle that privacy and real-time AML controls must coexist without centralised surveillance.

Validators evaluate a constant-time rule Valid(VI, CJT, ctx) ∈ {0,1}, where ctx includes asset type, network path, and time. Transactions that violate encoded policy constraints fail automatically before settlement. The protocol uses hybrid signatures (Ed25519 + Dilithium-III) for long-term post-quantum security without increasing latency. We formalize identity authenticity, policy-soundness, revocation-liveness, and ledger-anchored auditability, and show that violating any constraint reduces to signature forgery or hash-collision attacks. A prototype using eBPF/XDP achieves sub-5 ms validation (p95) and over ten million transactions per second, demonstrating feasibility for retail-scale CBDC systems.

Our results indicate that privacy, GDPR compliance, FATF alignment, and BIS-level financial-integrity objectives can be enforced simultaneously at the protocol layer. This creates a practical middle path between privacy-only CBDCs and surveillance-heavy architectures, enabling lawful, sovereign, and trust-preserving digital-currency infrastructures.

detail.title: Understanding Dairy Industry Innovation Ecosystem: Actor-Role Mapping and Systemic Problems in Indonesia
detail.abstract: This study examines the Indonesian dairy industry through the lens of innovation ecosystems, focusing on actor-role mapping and systemic problems undermining innovation and sustainability. Indonesia currently meets less than 21% of its domestic milk demand, indicating a critical gap in local capacity and governance. Using a qualitative research design, data were collected through semi-structured interviews with managers and staff from two key dairy cooperatives in Java, supplemented by secondary sources, including government policy reports and academic literature. The analysis was conducted using Gioia's methodology, combining inductive coding with deductive reasoning through an abductive approach. Findings reveal that key actors, including smallholder farmers, cooperatives, processors, NGOs, finance institutions, and government agencies, operate in silos, with minimal synergy or institutional integration. Critical challenges include limited value-added processing (less than 1% of raw milk), feed scarcity, inadequate downstream infrastructure, inactive cooperative associations (e.g., GKSI), uncoordinated public support, and short-term interventions by NGOs. The study concludes that institutional realignment, long-term policy frameworks, and actor coordination are crucial for building a resilient and inclusive innovation ecosystem that supports sustainable dairy development in Indonesia. These findings offer practical insights for enhancing governance, food security, and sustainability in the agricultural sectors of emerging economies

detail.title: Enhancing Financial Inclusion in Uzbekistan
detail.abstract: Financial inclusion plays a crucial role in promoting economic growth, particularly in developing countries like Uzbekistan, where a significant portion of the population is still financially excluded. This paper explores the current state of financial inclusion and how to enhance it in Uzbekistan, the study takes key factors such as banking penetration, access to credit, mobile banking usage, and financial literacy. The study uses qualitative and quantitative methods, primarily employing trend analysis to track changes in these indicators over time. Data was gathered from reputable sources, including the National Statistical Committee of Uzbekistan, the Ministry of Finance, the Central Bank, the World Bank, and the IMF. The qualitative analysis identifies barriers to financial inclusion, including gaps in financial literacy, infrastructure constraints, and regulatory challenges. Furthermore, the study evaluates government initiatives, such as the National Strategy for Financial Inclusion (2023-2025), and their impact on expanding access to financial services. The findings suggest that, despite progress, significant challenges remain in reaching underserved populations, particularly in rural areas. The paper concludes that addressing these barriers through technological advancements, policy reforms, and enhanced collaboration between the government, financial institutions, and NGOs could foster more inclusive financial services and contribute to long-term economic development.

detail.abstract: Economic crashes follow consistent patterns rooted in credit expansion, excessive debt accumulation, and cyclical overheating. This paper analyzes why economies crash using two primary frameworks: Clément Juglar's 7-11 year economic cycle theory and Ray Dalio's credit-based economic machine. Historical recession data from 1929 to 2020 is used to validate these theories. The findings show strong overlap: economic expansions create rising credit and confidence, leading to overheating, followed by credit tightening, panic, deleveraging, and recession. Juglar's cyclical view and Dalio's debt-cycle mechanics jointly explain the repetitive structure of economic crashes.

title: The Coexistence of Loss Aversion and Regret Aversion in Decision Making Under Risk

detail.title: The Coexistence of Loss Aversion and Regret Aversion in Decision Making Under Risk
detail.abstract: This paper explores the concurrent roles of prospect theory and regret theory in decision making under risk through a series of carefully designed experiments. We demonstrate that both models can be important for explaining real human choices in uncertain environments. Our experimental paradigm uses pairs of binary lotteries designed to induce both loss aversion and regret, with one gamble always involving a loss and the other changing from mixed, with both a gain and a loss, to gain only. Changes in behavior around these switching points elucidate loss aversion. Three feedback treatments are employed-no feedback, partial feedback (where only the chosen gamble's outcome is revealed), and complete feedback (where outcomes of both gambles are revealed)-to assess how different levels of information influence decision making. In the no feedback treatment, we find strong support for prospect theory. When feedback is introduced, participants' behavior reflects both prospect theory and regret theory although loss aversion has a greater impact than regret. Our findings underscore the importance of considering such hybrid models in evaluating decision making under risk, as well as the need to account for the information available to decision makers, as behavior varies with different feedback conditions.

title: Comparative Quality Assessment of the Systemic Risk of Doing Business (SRDB) Indicator with Dynamic Weights Against Established Macroeconomic Indicators

detail.title: Comparative Quality Assessment of the Systemic Risk of Doing Business (SRDB) Indicator with Dynamic Weights Against Established Macroeconomic Indicators
detail.abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive comparative quality assessment of the Systemic Risk of Doing Business (SRDB) indicator with time-varying weights against two established macroeconomic indicators: the Consumer Price Index (CPI) measuring inflation and Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measuring economic growth. Using a seven-dimensional evaluation framework consistent with European Statistical System (ESS) quality standards, we assess: (1) methodological rigor, (2) data quality and sources, (3) estimation transparency, (4) revision stability, (5) international comparability, (6) forecasting power, and (7) operational applicability. Key Findings: SRDB with dynamic weights achieves measurement quality comparable to or exceeding established indicators across most dimensions, while providing substantial advantages in forecasting power and operational lead time. Specifically: (1) Methodological Rigor: SRDB employs rigorous GMM estimation with Hansen J-test validation (all p>0.75), statespace Kalman filtering, and Markov-switching regime identification-methodologically superior to CPI's Laspeyres index and GDP's national accounts aggregation. (2) Data Quality: All three indicators rely on high-quality administrative and market data; SRDB uses real-time financial market prices with minimal lag. (3) Transparency: SRDB methodology fully reproducible from published specifications; CPI and GDP involve substantial discretionary adjustments. (4) Revisions: SRDB exhibits minimal revisions (market data rarely revised) compared to GDP mean absolute revisions of 0.3-0.7 percentage points and CPI seasonal adjustments. (5) International Comparability: All three indicators achieve excellent crosscountry comparability. (6) Forecasting Power: SRDB demonstrates 18.6-24.4% RMSE improvement over fixed-weight specifications; 44% improvement during crisis periods-no forecasting capability exists for CPI or GDP. (7) Lead Time: SRDB provides 6-15 month forward-looking signals; CPI and GDP are purely backward-looking with 1-3 month publication lags. Conclusion: SRDB with dynamic weights represents a paradigm advancement in macroeconomic measurement, achieving traditional indicator robustness while providing forecasting capabilities absent from established measures. The indicator is ready for operational deployment alongside CPI and GDP in central bank monitoring frameworks.

detail.abstract: This study is the first modeling academic career progression using multi-state models, an approach that allows to compute additional quantities of interest never produced in this context, such as the probability of attaining specific academic positions over given time horizons and the average time required to reach them. Potential gender differences along these dimensions are assessed by comparing these metrics computed for male and female scholars separately, while accounting for productivity, individual preferences, and even seniority, which are often cited as explanations for women's disadvantage in academic careers. Leveraging a suitably-built highly informative dataset covering the universe of professors having worked in Italian universities between 2016 and 2021, we show a gap in the probabilities of career advancement that reduces with the career horizon but never vanishes, stabilizing around 2 (3) percentage points for those starting their career as Assistant (Associate) professors. In addition, we find that female scholars require up to two additional years to reach the highest academic rank (full professorship) compared with otherwise equivalent male counterparts, a phenomenon we label the "pink queue". Finally, we find a systematic misalignment in career advancement probabilities between male and female scholars with comparable productivity, whereby women achieve the same advancement chances as men only when they attain higher productivity levels, suggesting the presence of a potential "double standard".

title: Robustness of Benefit of the Doubt in Energy Management Performance Assessment: A Hit-and-Run Randomized Weights Approach Across 174 Countries

detail.title: Robustness of Benefit of the Doubt in Energy Management Performance Assessment: A Hit-and-Run Randomized Weights Approach Across 174 Countries
detail.abstract: The Benefit-of-the-Doubt (BoD) model offers a flexible, data-driven alternative to rigid weighting schemes for assessing national energy management performance (EMP), but its optimization structure can lead to overestimated performance. This study introduces a novel hybrid approach combining BoD with Hit-and-Run (H&R) randomized sampling to enhance assessment robustness. The methodology was applied to 174 countries using 13 energy indicators from 2022. First, conventional BoD scores were calculated. Then, 100,000 H&R simulations per country were performed, adhering to BoD constraints including a 0.02 minimum indicator weight, to explore the entire feasible weight space. This generated a distribution of possible scores and rankings for each country. Statistical comparison revealed that conventional BoD scores exhibited a consistent upward bias, averaging 0.2381 higher than mean H&R scores (p < 0.001, t(173) = 50.82). While overall rank correlation between the two assessment methods remained strong (Spearman's ρ ≈ 0.934), significant rank fluctuations were observed for many countries, with a maximum downward shift of 111 positions. The analysis allowed for the identification of countries whose performance evaluations were highly sensitive to specific weighting configurations versus those with more stable evaluations. This BoD-H&R framework provides a more dependable method for international energy benchmarking by quantifying and mitigating optimism bias and offering policymakers a clearer view of comparative performance.

detail.abstract: This research examines Green Service Quality (GSQ) as a key factor in increasing tourist satisfaction and the competitiveness of sustainable tourism destinations in Indonesia. GSQ encompasses tangibility, reliability, responsiveness, assurance, and empathy, with a strong emphasis on sustainability. The main dimensions of GSQ identified include hotel eco-centricity, staff attitudes towards sustainability, facility quality, location, service character, perceived value, and intention to revisit. The method used is qualitative research with a literature review technique. The findings indicate that the dimensions of tangibility, reliability, responsiveness, and empathy have a significant impact on visit intention and tourist satisfaction. At the same time, assurance tends to be insignificant in some segments, especially among Generation Z. Visible, well-functioning GSQ practices become a factor of delight that exceeds basic service expectations, strengthening the guest experience and supporting sustainable tourism development goals. The integration of GSQ into hotel operational strategies through green facility design, environmentally friendly standard procedures, staff training, and certification mechanisms can increase tourist satisfaction, loyalty, and intentions to recommend.

detail.abstract: This paper discusses the importance of emotional control for professional poker players, focusing on how variance-both positive and negative-affects decision-making, a phenomenon commonly known as *tilt*, and on the relevance of bankroll management in maintaining optimal decision quality during extended periods of negative variance. The article reviews theoretical and empirical evidence, including the work of authors such as Jared Tendler and Maria Konnikova, and recommends practices for preventing and recovering from *tilt*. It emphasizes that financial discipline and mental training are complementary and essential for the long-term sustainability of a winning player.

detail.abstract: This study investigates how strategic leadership, organizational orientation, and technological capabilities interact to drive disruptive innovation within an emerging-market tourism context. Drawing on Strategic Contingency Theory, Upper Echelons Theory, and the Resource-Based View, we develop and empirically test an integrated model using data from 88 Vietnamese tourism firms through Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The results reveal that transformational leadership and strategic orientation significantly foster an innovation-supportive organizational culture, which in turn mediates their effects on disruptive innovation. Technological capabilities contribute indirectly, exerting influence only when aligned with a collaborative and adaptive cultural environment. These findings underscore organizational culture as the critical strategic mechanism through which leadership vision and strategic intent are converted into technological and innovation outcomes. The study advances the literature on technology and innovation management by situating disruptive innovation within service-based, emerging-economy industries. Practically, it offers guidance for managers and policymakers seeking to strengthen technological transformation and innovation capacity through culturally embedded strategic alignment.

title: Neural Correlates of Existential Engagement: A Conceptual and Computational Model of First-Person Reflection versus Analytical Detachment

detail.title: Neural Correlates of Existential Engagement: A Conceptual and Computational Model of First-Person Reflection versus Analytical Detachment
detail.abstract: This paper presents a theoretical and computational framework for exploring the dynamics of first-person reflective cognition versus analytical detachment. We model the interactions of key neural networks-Default Mode Network (DMN), Central Executive Network (CEN), and Salience Network (SN)-as a stochastic dynamical system, from which emergent cognitive modes E(t) (reflective engagement) and A(t) (analytical processing) arise. Hybrid states, identified conceptually as x d ≈ x e , capture moments of co-activation between these modes, suggesting a dynamic interplay between introspection and detachment. Sensitivity and phase-plane analyses reveal regions of heightened responsiveness and potential hybrid cognition, offering insights into how parameter variations influence cognitive stability. Importantly, all results are derived theoretically, based on the analytical structure of the governing equations; no empirical simulations were performed. This framework bridges computational neuroscience and philosophical inquiry, providing a formalized model to interpret the oscillatory tension between subjective reflection and objective analysis, and highlighting the potential for theoretical models to illuminate the architecture of human cognition.

title: An Inevitable Winter? Forecasting Indian Private Equity Alpha by Comparing the U.S. Historical Precedent

detail.title: An Inevitable Winter? Forecasting Indian Private Equity Alpha by Comparing the U.S. Historical Precedent
detail.abstract: As Indian Private Equity experiences record capital inflows, investors question the sustainability of excess returns. This paper forecasts market maturity by benchmarking Indian PE market (2014-2024) against the historical U.S. cycle (1984-2008). Reconstructing a longitudinal dataset of capital commitments and deal typologies reveals that India's "Buyout Share" has expanded from 6.6% in 2014 to ~34.7% in 2024. Structurally, this mirrors the U.S. market of 1983-1984, immediately preceding its "Golden Age" of performance. Contrary to overheating concerns, findings suggest that there is a structural alpha runway of at least 4-5 years exists before market saturation through hypercapitalization (70% buyout concentration) triggers alpha fade and sub-par returns.

detail.abstract: Developing nations in the 21st century have undergone profound changes amid accelerating globalization, technological advances, and evolving policy paradigms. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the transformations and challenges facing developing countries – with a special focus on Africa – and outlines pathways to sustainable and inclusive growth. We review economic transformation trends, highlighting both robust growth and persistent structural weaknesses, and examine societal development progress in areas such as education, health, and poverty reduction. We explore how many low- and middle-income countries are leapfrogging technologically, adopting digital innovations to overcome infrastructure gaps, and we assess efforts at structural modernization through industrial policy and diversification. Key thematic sections analyze demographic dynamics (e.g. rapid population growth and urbanization), industrial policy and structural change (including the return of industrial strategies and the risk of premature deindustrialization), digital transformation (mobile technology, internet access, and innovation), urbanization (the rise of mega-cities and urban challenges), climate and sustainability constraints (climate change impacts and green growth imperatives), human capital development (education and health systems outcomes), and financial inclusion (the expansion of banking, mobile money, and poverty reduction strategies). Across these themes, regional nuances are emphasized – particularly Africa’s trajectory, which features the world’s fastest population growth and some of its toughest development hurdles. Drawing on global data sets, academic literature, and development policy frameworks (from the Millennium Development Goals to the Sustainable Development Goals and Africa’s Agenda 2063), we ground the analysis in evidence. We find that while the 21st century has seen remarkable progress – such as a dramatic fall in extreme poverty globally and improvements in health and education – developing nations continue to face multidimensional challenges including incomplete economic structural transformation, climate vulnerabilities, governance and institutional capacity gaps, and rising inequality. The paper concludes with future projections and policy pathways for sustainable and inclusive development. These include harnessing the demographic dividend through investments in education and jobs, promoting industrial diversification and digital innovation, strengthening institutions and governance, expanding social protection and financial inclusion, and securing climate resilience. Achieving sustainable growth will require integrated strategies and global cooperation, but with the right policies, developing regions – especially Africa – can make decisive strides toward inclusive prosperity in the coming decades.

detail.abstract: Allelopathy refers to a biological phenomenon in which one plant releases biochemicals that influence the germination and growth of neighbouring plants. This study evaluated the allelopathic potential of two common weeds, Euphorbia helioscopia L. and Oxalis corniculata L., on the germination and early growth of Triticum aestivum L. The experiment was conducted under a completely randomised design (CRD) with three replications per treatment. Aqueous extracts were prepared from fresh shoots and roots at concentrations of 5%, 10%, and 15% (w/v), while dry plant material was mixed with sterile sand for mulching treatments. A distilled water control was included. Germination and growth parameters were recorded after 72 hours of incubation at 25 °C. Results indicated that aqueous extracts from both weeds significantly (p < 0.05) reduced wheat germination percentage, plumule and radicle length, and root number compared with the control. However, low concentrations (5%) and mixed shoot extracts exhibited mild stimulatory effects, increasing radicle length to 6.2 cm and plumule length to 9.0 cm, compared with 5.3 cm and 6.6 cm in the control, respectively. Mulching treatments consistently inhibited germination and seedling growth, except the mixed treatment, which slightly enhanced leaf area (2.1 cm² vs. 1.5 cm² in the control). These findings suggest that E. helioscopia and O. corniculata produce bioactive compounds that can suppress wheat germination and growth. Their strong allelopathic potential warrants further investigation for possible applications in natural weed and pest management.

title: A Cyclical Structural Analysis of U.S. Nuclear Power Outages (2015-2023) Using the Adhishthana Principles

detail.title: A Cyclical Structural Analysis of U.S. Nuclear Power Outages (2015-2023) Using the Adhishthana Principles
detail.abstract:
Nuclear power remains a critical component of the United States energy infrastructure, yet outages, arising from weather disturbances, equipment failures, grid instability, and other systemic events, continue to present operational and forecasting challenges. This study applies the Adhishthana Principles, a structural analytical framework composed of eighteen cyclical phases, to U.S. nuclear outage data from 2015 to 2023 in order to identify recurring patterns that are not easily captured through event-specific or statistical methods. Using aggregated monthly outage counts derived from the EAGLE-I based Event-Correlated Outage Dataset, we examined year-by-year outage trajectories and mapped them onto the Adhishthana cycle.

Across all nine years of data, outages exhibited a consistent structural formation: a Cākra between Phases 4 and 8, followed by a decisive transition in Phase 9. In most years, this transition resulted in a breakdown of the Cākra and initiated the Move of Pralayā, with outage counts falling sharply in accordance with Adhishthana expectations. Detailed analyses of the 2016 and 2019 datasets illustrate this behavior, with post-breakdown declines of 41.87% and 48.15%, respectively. While the present study focuses on the Cākra-Pralayā sequence, the results indicate that additional insights may be obtained through finer-grained analyses of plant-level data and other phases within the Adhishthana framework.

The findings demonstrate that nuclear outages in the United States conform to a recurring cyclical rhythm, suggesting the presence of an underlying structural pattern independent of specific outage causes. These results highlight the potential value of the Adhishthana Principles as a complementary tool for interpreting outage behavior and improving the anticipatory capabilities of nuclear grid operators and policymakers. Future work incorporating micro-level data and phase-specific modeling may further enhance the predictive utility of this approach.

detail.abstract: The changing contours of judicial intervention in arbitral awards under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, against the background of the recent Supreme Court ruling in Gayatri Balasamy v. ISG Novasoft Technologies Ltd. has been analyzed. At the heart of the article is the question whether Indian courts can revise arbitral awards or whether their scope is restricted to setting them aside. Charting the historical development from the expansive discretion under the 1940 Act to the restricted, restrained role outlined by the 1996 Act, the article examines how courts have interpreted the limits of their supervisory jurisdiction. Through detailed reading of seminal precedents-Hakeem, McDermott, and Ssangyong, this paper places the Balasamy ruling in the context of a shift in doctrine that cautiously reopens the door to limited modifications in rare cases, e.g., severable awards or clerical mistakes. The article contends that although Balasamy does not fully overturn the dominant restrictive reading of Section 34, it proposes a realistic exception that promises sagacious future development. In doing so, the ruling takes a middle path between safeguarding arbitral finality and permitting limited corrective discretion to courts.

detail.abstract: Tokenized stocks-blockchain-based representations of traditional equities-are reshaping how markets incorporate information. They enable continuous 24/7 trading, global accessibility to several trading platforms, and fractional ownership. Leveraging a novel dataset covering the hundreds of tokenized stocks launched since July 2025, we provide the first empirical assessment of this market, with a focus on price discovery under continuous fractional trading. While token markets remain small ($420M market cap), they exhibit intriguing dynamics: (i) prices track the underlying closely during regular hours but deviate modestly overnight and on weekends; (ii) weekend trading redistributes the traditional Monday return, anticipating rather than amplifying it; (iii) micro-trades under $100-enabled by fractionalizationoccur at high volume without persistent mispricing, suggesting effective arbitrage; and (iv) off-hour token returns exhibit short-horizon reversals, offering new insights into how markets process information when only one trading venue is open. Our results provide an early empirical assessment of tokenized stocks, offering insights with broad implications for market efficiency, information disclosure, and investor access as traditional equity exposure migrates to fast-growing crypto markets.

This paper examines the current landscape of AI and data utilization in African fintech, analyzing both the unprecedented opportunities created by technological leapfrogging and the unique challenges posed by infrastructure, regulatory, and socioeconomic constraints. detail.title: Decolonising Leadership Assessment: The Reveal Yourself® Framework as an Afrocentric Alternative to Western Psychometrics
detail.abstract: Western leadership assessments, such as the MBTI, DISC, and Hogan, dominate global practice. However, their cultural bias and questionable validity have prompted calls to decolonise psychometrics. This white paper introduces Reveal Yourself®, an Afrocentric leadership assessment framework designed as an alternative to Western tools. We detail its development, rooted in African cultural paradigms and archetypes, and present a pilot study with emerging African leaders. Results indicate that Reveal Yourself® achieves high cultural coherence; participants found the archetypal profiles authentic to their lived experiences, enhancing self-awareness and perceived leadership effectiveness. We compare Reveal Yourself® with established instruments (Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI), DISC, Hogan) in terms of design origin, cultural relevance, validation, and delivery model, highlighting the new framework's distinctive positioning. An initial conceptual model is proposed, linking culturally aligned leadership archetypes to improved leadership outcomes. Ethical considerations of the pilot, including informed consent and confidentiality measures, are discussed, despite the absence of formal institutional ethics approval. Lastly, we outline a strategy for commercialising Reveal Yourself® as a digital tool with certified facilitation and invite partnerships with universities, funders, and leadership institutes to collaboratively validate and expand this Afrocentric innovation. detail.abstract: This article advances cycle symbiosis as a novel AI-enabled framework for predicting, mitigating, and recovering from e-commerce cycles, drawing empirical lessons from the 2022-2023 global downturn to formulate strategies for durable resilience in transnational markets. Within a sector exceeding USD 6 trillion in 2025 (McKinsey, 2025) yet increasingly exposed to disruptions that suppress global GDP by up to 1.5% (World Bank, 2023), the central problem addressed is the limited integration of AI-based prediction with cyclical dynamics. Existing scholarship foregrounds structural adaptations in global value chains (Gereffi, 2020) but seldom examines how predictive intelligence and entrepreneurial agency interact symbiotically to generate multiplicative value in high-volatility contexts. Anchored in global value chain (GVC) theory, post-crisis economics (IMF, 2025), the resource-based view (RBV; Barney, 1991), and dynamic capabilities (Teece, 2014), this study conceptualizes cycle symbiosis as a sequence of interdependent AI-loops that synchronize sensing, prediction, adaptation, and reinvestment. Using a mixed-methods design that combines a single-case qualitative study (Yin, 2018) with quantitative components audited financial data and 2025 industry benchmarks from Omnisend and Klaviyo the analysis examines a transnational e-commerce venture operating across divergent institutional environments. Findings indicate 15-25% improvements in predictive accuracy, enabling strategic actions that yielded 277% year-over-year growth (exceeding Omnisend's 12.6% benchmark), 38.8% customer retention (surpassing Klaviyo's 25-30% norm), a USD 172 average order value (19% above industry averages), and 1:3 economic multipliers generating over USD 1.5 million annually through salaries, tax contributions, and R&D investments. These outcomes empirically validate the model's hypotheses, illustrating how cycle symbiosis mitigates contractionary shocks such as the 6.5% spending decline documented in 2022 (FXC Intelligence, 2023), while advancing socially sustainable development in origin and host markets. The study contributes theoretically by extending GVC frameworks to incorporate AI as a symbiotic predictor and by repositioning transnational entrepreneurs as stabilizing agents within cyclical environments. Practically, it offers a structured roadmap for small and medium-sized transnational enterprises to operationalize cycle symbiosis. Policy implications include the potential to scale this model into state-supported export and innovation hubs capable of unlocking significant macroeconomic value. Limitations inherent to the single-case design suggest the need for longitudinal, multi-country, and sector-variable investigations. Overall, the findings position cycle symbiosis as a scalable paradigm for resilient, AI-enabled value creation in global e-commerce ecosystems.

detail.abstract: Consensus protocols used today in blockchains mostly rely on scarce resources such as computational power or financial stake, favoring wealthy individuals due to a high entry barrier. We propose Proof-of-Social-Capital (PoSC), a new consensus protocol fueled by social capital as a staking resource to ensure fairness and decentralization. Consensus nodes in our system do not require financial nor computational resources that are expensive to acquire; instead, they utilize preexisting social media influence, distributing consensus power not according to wealth but social capital. Our approach integrates zkSNARK proofs, verifiable credentials with a uniqueness-enforcing mechanism to prevent Sybil attacks, and the incentive scheme that rewards engagement with social media content by followers. This work offers a new concept aligned with modern social media lifestyle applied in finance, providing a practical insight for evolution of decentralized consensus protocols.

detail.abstract: Our practical question is the following: can regime-based models based on Hidden Markov Models reduce risk exposure while remaining competitive? Our four approaches are based on a volatility-regime architecture with a simple defensive overlay: • Model 1: PCA–HMM (Hard Regime) uses the cross-asset structure (princi pal components) to estimate discrete regimes. • Model 2: Prob–HMM (Soft) + Momentum Sleeve blends per-regime assignments via one-step-ahead probabilities and adds a stress-gated momentum sleeve. • Model 3: Regime-Aware HRP Conditions (RAHC) applies hierarchical risk parity under regime-conditioned covariances to stabilize risk contributions. • Model 4: IA + HMM Fusion is an interpretable HMM augmented with a lightweight inference-assist that tempers regime probabilities. Between models we apply equalizing controls (like data windows, rebalance fre quency, constraints, and transaction-cost hypotheses) and risk-coherent comparisons (e.g., volatility targeting) to attribute contributions to drawdown mitigation, tail-risk management, and weight stability. The question is: how much risk mitigation can interpretable regime-conscious approaches provide to institutional portfolios? For statisticians, financial engineers, and risk managers, we offer (i) a mathe matically grounded algorithmization of four HMM-based designs (hard/soft regimes, regime-conditioned risk parity, IA fusion) and (ii) a deployment-friendly assessment scheme (robustness, interpretability, governance). We find that regime awareness can improve risk discipline (drawdowns, tails, risk budgets) without unduly sacrificing Sharpe ratios.

detail.title: Borrower’s Microcredit Preferences: A Conjoint Analysis
detail.abstract: Microcredit, a financial innovation that provides small loans to individuals who lack access to traditional banking services, has emerged as a vital tool for promoting financial inclusion and supporting micro-entrepreneurship. This study investigated the microcredit preferences of borrowers in Dipolog City, Zamboanga del Norte, through a full-profile conjoint analysis. The objectives were to determine the relative importance of each attribute, estimate the utility scores of loan attribute levels, identify the most preferred loan profile, and simulate predicted market shares of existing microcredit providers. Four key attributes: loan amount, loan term, interest rate, and repayment frequency were identified through key informant interviews with 20 borrowers and validated by four microcredit provider managers. Using a fractional factorial design, 16 loan profiles were generated and rated by 200 microcredit borrowers on a five-point rating scale. Findings revealed that interest rate was the most influential attribute (34.9%), followed by repayment frequency (30.7%), loan amount (16.1%), and loan term (15.2%). Contrary to conventional expectations, the findings revealed that borrowers favored higher interest rates, likely due to their prioritization of larger loan amounts and their actual credit experiences. The most preferred loan profile featured a high loan amount (over Php 30,000), a short term (3 months), a high interest rate (over 2% per month), and a daily repayment frequency. Market simulations suggested that providers whose loan features closely matched borrower preferences likely achieve greater market shares. These results emphasize the importance of borrower-centered product design and offer strategic insights for microcredit provider institutions aiming to enhance outreach and client satisfaction in emerging economies.

title: Location-Robust Cost-Preserving Blended Pricing for Multi-Campus AI Data Centers

detail.title: Location-Robust Cost-Preserving Blended Pricing for Multi-Campus AI Data Centers
detail.abstract:
Large-scale AI data center portfolios procure identical SKUs across geographically heterogeneous campuses, yet finance and operations require a single system-level "world price" per SKU for budgeting and planning. A common practice is deployment-weighted blending of campus prices, which preserves total cost but can trigger Simpson-type aggregation failures: heterogeneous location mixes can reverse SKU rankings and distort decision signals.

I formalize cost-preserving blended pricing under location heterogeneity and propose two practical operators that reconcile accounting identity with ranking robustness and production implementability. A two-way fixed-effects operator separates global SKU effects from campus effects and restores exact cost preservation via scalar normalization, providing interpretable decomposition and smoothing under mild missingness. A convex common-weight operator computes a single set of campus weights under accounting constraints to enforce a location-robust benchmark and prevent dominance reversals; I also provide feasibility diagnostics and a slack-based fallback for extreme mix conditions. Simulations and an AI data center OPEX illustration show substantial reductions in ranking violations relative to naive blending while maintaining cost accuracy, with scalable distributed implementation.

detail.abstract:
The Performance Efficiency Index (PEI) is an advanced analytical framework designed to optimize asset performance in capital-intensive industries. By integrating data-driven diagnostics with economic evaluation, the PEI determines the optimal timing for equipment maintenance, ensuring operational reliability while minimizing financial deviation from planned budgets. Its proactive structure enables organizations to anticipate deteriorating performance, adjust maintenance schedules, and intervene before critical failures occur, reducing downtime and maximizing operational continuity.

Beyond its predictive maintenance capabilities, the PEI functions as a comprehensive decision-making tool that incorporates financial modeling, scenario analysis, and risk assessment. This dual technical-economic approach enhances resource allocation, strengthens asset protection, and supports organizations in maintaining alignment with strategic performance objectives in dynamic market environments. Seamlessly integrated into existing maintenance protocols, the model adds an economic layer that improves the precision and strategic value of routine operational decisions.

The PEI was originally developed and applied in the downstream segment of the Oil & Gas industry, specifically within the Coker Unit of the Petrocedeño upgrader refinery in Venezuela. This unit, highly sensitive to operational and thermal variables, provided a challenging yet impactful testing environment for the model. Through early detection of performance decline—supported by acoustic ultrasound testing that revealed skin formation and drum cracking—the PEI guided management to accelerate a major maintenance shutdown. The intervention yielded a net recovered profit of USD 11.7 million in the first month, with an estimated additional USD 21 million projected for the following month, totaling USD 32.8 million in economic benefit. The analysis also demonstrated that forecasting beyond 60 days becomes unreliable due to accelerated performance degradation, reinforcing the model’s emphasis on short-term predictive accuracy.

With its combined focus on operational efficiency and financial optimization, the PEI demonstrates strong potential to transform maintenance planning and long-term asset management. Although originally tailored for Oil & Gas operations, its methodology—rooted in predictive analytics, financial indicators, and proactive risk mitigation—makes the PEI a scalable and versatile tool applicable across multiple sectors, including renewable energy systems such as solar farm infrastructure. This adaptability positions the Performance Efficiency Index as a significant contribution to modern industrial asset management and strategic financial planning.

detail.abstract:
The Renewable Energy Sustainable Investment (RESI) project is a strategic initiative designed to accelerate the adoption of renewable energy in the United States, with a specific focus on low-income and Native American tribal communities that face disproportionate energy costs and limited access to affordable electricity. By integrating federal funding opportunities, financial modeling, and private–public collaboration, RESI aims to reduce energy poverty, stimulate local economic development, and support the national transition toward a resilient, low-carbon energy system.

The project begins with a comprehensive evaluation of federal grants and incentive programs offered by agencies such as the Department of Energy (DOE), Department of Interior (DOI), Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Department of Agriculture (USDA), and the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). This assessment supports the development of data-driven proposals that leverage governmental tools, financial expertise, and investment planning to deploy large-scale renewable energy installations—primarily solar farms—near communities in need of clean, affordable power.

RESI highlights the economic and operational advantages of utility-scale solar farms over residential rooftop systems. Solar farms exhibit significantly lower installation costs per watt, require no rooftop restrictions, and generate greater electricity output due to scalable land availability. They also create opportunities for landowners to lease land profitably and for investors to participate in renewable energy real-estate development. Their deployment not only reduces reliance on fossil fuels but also enhances regional resilience and energy security for the United States.

A central component of the RESI model is the integration of financial projections that quantify community benefits, including substantial reductions in energy bills, job creation, and long-term economic stimulation. By enabling cooperative ownership structures, community shares, and equitable investment participation, RESI ensures that local residents benefit directly from renewable energy assets. These mechanisms promote energy independence, strengthen community governance, and enhance social equity by empowering disadvantaged populations.

In addition to the environmental gains, the RESI framework emphasizes the socioeconomic impact of renewable energy adoption in underserved areas. The project demonstrates how solar and wind installations can reduce utility expenses, increase household economic stability, and support local economic diversification. Through targeted deployment guided by federal data—such as utility-scale solar maps from the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA)—RESI prioritizes regions with the greatest need and potential impact.

Overall, the Renewable Energy Sustainable Investment (RESI) project represents an integrated, scalable, and financially sustainable model that connects federal incentives, investors, landowners, and vulnerable communities. By aligning clean energy development with social equity and economic opportunity, RESI provides a pathway for the United States to expand renewable energy capacity while uplifting the communities that need it most.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether the cartel's effects persist after the sanction period ends. We use the JATO database to construct transaction-level prices for identical car models in a cartel-affected market (Spain) and a comparable benchmark market (Germany) that was not subject to the cartel. Tracking pre-, during-, and post-sanction periods at a highly granular product level allows us to directly test whether overcharges persist once sanctions are lifted-an empirical setting in which the literature has long warned of bias yet has lacked cross-market, model-matched transaction data. Abstract
Social media in B2B business development has received limited academic attention compared to its extensive treatment in B2C contexts. This doctoral research examines how social media influences the B2B business development process within global software solutions and services firms. Using a mixed-methods design grounded in post-positivism, the study develops and tests a conceptual model informed by relationship marketing, information systems theory, social capital, and usage criteria.
The research combines qualitative insights from expert interviews across functions, industries, and regions with a large-scale cross-sectional survey of more than 530 practitioners drawn from LinkedIn and XING. Measurement instruments were derived from existing literature and refined through exploratory and confirmatory analyses, including thematic analysis and structural equation modelling.
The findings suggest that digital and social media accelerate the B2B business development process cycle: by enhancing visibility, strengthening relational ties, and supporting cross-functional cooperation. Social media acts as a subsidiary technology that reduces information asymmetry and improves perceived business performance, though its impact should not be overstated. The study contributes a parsimonious, innovative model that integrates social media into B2B business development, highlights the moderating role of social capital, and proposes new constructs, including the Social Business Relevance and Social Business Motivation Indices. Managerial implications include classifying B2B developers into social media advocates, mixed types, and sceptics, and offering guidelines to render business development operations more agile and collaborative.

title: AI as a Catalyst: Uncovering the Effects of AI Assistance on Review Generation and Engagement

detail.title: AI as a Catalyst: Uncovering the Effects of AI Assistance on Review Generation and Engagement
detail.abstract: Public opinion is vital for societies and markets, yet the "silent majority" often hesitates to share views. This study examines how generative AI can facilitate opinion expression. Building on a custom video platform, we experimentally tested two formats of AI assistance powered by large language models: a one-click generation from user-provided keywords or prompts, and an interactive chatbot for collaborative drafting. Four key findings emerge. First, AI assistance boosts comment rates by 15.19% over the plain control without AI. This effect is particularly pronounced among those typically reluctant to review online. Second, AI-assisted comments exhibit systematic positive sentiment bias. Third, with a follow-up study to solicit genuine opinions of the same users, we find that, surprisingly, AI-assisted comments are more semantically similar to these genuine opinions (via text embeddings). Fourth, we find that these AI-assisted comments can drive downstream user engagement via richer informational content. To explain these findings, we propose, and find evidence for, a sequential model of the cognitive writing process: users articulate aspects of their opinion with costly effort and may stop early; AI enhances efficiency by helping users expand the key aspects for expression, despite biased sentiment. These results highlight generative AI's potential to promote broader, authentic opinion sharing and consumer engagement, while noting bias risks for platform design.

detail.abstract: This paper provides new cross-country evidence that greater investment in agricultural R&D significantly mitigates the adverse effects of climate variability on crop yields in sub-Saharan Africa. Despite this critical role, only a handful of countries have invested at levels sufficient to reach the thresholds where R&D delivers effective risk adaptation. Our analysis indicates that closing this gap would require an additional US$1–3 billion in annual agricultural research investment across the region.
